"""Signing records for each dataset, and SSH signatures over them.

The paper has its own attestation protocol (docs/contrapunctus-attest.md). This
is the same mechanism for the corpora: OpenSSH Ed25519 signatures
(`ssh-keygen -Y`), in a separate namespace, `anthropic-pbc-dataset`, so a
dataset signature can never be replayed as an endorsement of the paper.

A record lists, for one dataset in corpus/datasets.tsv:
  - the BLAKE3 of every committed file in its corpus folder;
  - the BLAKE3 of every script its refresh command runs;
  - what a signature over the record attests.
It holds no clock and no commit id, so it is a pure function of the files. When
any file changes, the record changes, and an old signature stops verifying: the
dataset shows as stale until someone re-signs.

    uv run scripts/attest_datasets.py record                 # write attestations/datasets/<id>.txt
    uv run scripts/attest_datasets.py sign --key ~/.ssh/KEY --signer "NAME"   # run by the signer
    uv run scripts/attest_datasets.py verify                 # exit 1 on a bad or stale signature
    uv run scripts/attest_datasets.py status                 # signed / unsigned / stale per dataset

`sign` runs `verify` for each dataset's own build first (`<script> verify`),
when the script has one, and refuses to sign a record that is not current.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import blake3

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
REGISTRY = ROOT / "corpus" / "datasets.tsv"
DIR = ROOT / "attestations" / "datasets"
ALLOWED = ROOT / "attestations" / "allowed_signers"
NAMESPACE = "anthropic-pbc-dataset"
STATEMENT = (
    "By signing this record, the signer attests that, when they signed: the files listed\n"
    "had exactly these BLAKE3 hashes; the dataset's own verify step (where it has one)\n"
    "passed; and the files are the output of the listed scripts run on the sources\n"
    "pinned in the dataset's MANIFEST.tsv. It does not attest that any finding drawn\n"
    "from the dataset is true, and it says nothing about model output in proposals/.\n")


def b3(p: Path) -> str:
    return blake3.blake3(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def registry() -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    return [r for r in csv.DictReader(REGISTRY.open(), delimiter="\t") if r["corpus_dir"] != "—"]


def scripts_of(r: dict[str, str]) -> list[str]:
    return sorted(set(re.findall(r"scripts/[\w./-]+\.py", r["refresh"])))


def tracked(folder: str) -> list[str]:
    out = subprocess.run(["git", "ls-files", "-z", "--", folder], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, check=True).stdout
    return sorted(p for p in out.decode().split("\0") if p)


def render(r: dict[str, str]) -> str:
    lines = [f"namespace: {NAMESPACE}", f"dataset: {r['id']}", f"title: {r['title']}",
             f"pinned_as_of: {r['pinned_as_of']}", f"registry: corpus/datasets.tsv", "",
             STATEMENT, "files (BLAKE3, path):"]
    for p in tracked(r["corpus_dir"]):
        lines.append(f"{b3(ROOT / p)}  {p}")
    lines += ["", "scripts (BLAKE3, path):"]
    for p in scripts_of(r):
        lines.append(f"{b3(ROOT / p)}  {p}")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def cmd_record(_a) -> int:
    DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for r in registry():
        (DIR / f"{r['id']}.txt").write_text(render(r))
    print(f"wrote {len(registry())} records to {DIR.relative_to(ROOT)}/")
    return 0


def status() -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """(dataset, signed | unsigned | stale | bad-signature)."""
    res = []
    for r in registry():
        rec, sig = DIR / f"{r['id']}.txt", DIR / f"{r['id']}.txt.sig"
        current = rec.exists() and rec.read_text() == render(r)
        if not sig.exists():
            res.append((r["id"], "unsigned" if current else "unsigned, record stale"))
            continue
        if not current:
            res.append((r["id"], "stale (files changed since signing)"))
            continue
        signer = sig.with_suffix(".signer").read_text().strip() if sig.with_suffix(".signer").exists() else ""
        ok = subprocess.run(["ssh-keygen", "-Y", "verify", "-f", str(ALLOWED), "-I", signer, "-n", NAMESPACE,
                             "-s", str(sig)], input=rec.read_bytes(), capture_output=True).returncode == 0
        res.append((r["id"], f"signed by {signer}" if ok else "bad signature"))
    return res


def cmd_status(_a) -> int:
    for d, s in status():
        print(f"{d:20} {s}")
    return 0


def cmd_verify(_a) -> int:
    bad = [(d, s) for d, s in status() if s.startswith(("stale", "bad"))]
    for d, s in bad:
        print(f"FAIL {d}: {s}")
    print("ok" if not bad else f"{len(bad)} dataset(s) failed")
    return 1 if bad else 0


def cmd_sign(a) -> int:
    if "\n" in a.signer or '"' in a.signer:
        sys.exit("signer name must be one line without quotes")
    key = Path(a.key).expanduser()
    pub = key.with_suffix(key.suffix + ".pub") if not key.name.endswith(".pub") else key
    if not pub.exists():
        sys.exit(f"no public key at {pub}")
    ids = [x for x in a.datasets] or [r["id"] for r in registry()]
    for r in registry():
        if r["id"] not in ids:
            continue
        rec = DIR / f"{r['id']}.txt"
        if not rec.exists() or rec.read_text() != render(r):
            sys.exit(f"{r['id']}: record is missing or stale; run `record` and commit it first")
        for s in scripts_of(r):
            src = (ROOT / s).read_text()
            if '"verify"' in src or "'verify'" in src:
                print(f"{r['id']}: {s} verify ...", flush=True)
                if subprocess.run(["uv", "run", s, "verify"], cwd=ROOT).returncode != 0:
                    sys.exit(f"{r['id']}: {s} verify failed; not signing")
        sig = rec.with_suffix(".txt.sig")
        sig.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        # ssh-keygen reads the private key itself (or the agent); no key material passes through here.
        if subprocess.run(["ssh-keygen", "-Y", "sign", "-f", str(key), "-n", NAMESPACE, str(rec)]).returncode != 0:
            sys.exit(f"{r['id']}: ssh-keygen sign failed")
        rec.with_suffix(".txt.signer").write_text(a.signer + "\n")
    # add the signer to allowed_signers once
    line = f'"{a.signer}" namespaces="{NAMESPACE}" ' + " ".join(pub.read_text().split()[:2])
    have = ALLOWED.read_text().splitlines() if ALLOWED.exists() else []
    if line not in have:
        ALLOWED.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        ALLOWED.write_text("\n".join(have + [line]) + "\n")
    return cmd_status(a)


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    sub.add_parser("record")
    sub.add_parser("status")
    sub.add_parser("verify")
    s = sub.add_parser("sign")
    s.add_argument("--key", required=True, help="path to your SSH private key (ssh-keygen reads it; agent keys work)")
    s.add_argument("--signer", required=True, help='name recorded in allowed_signers, e.g. "Sloane Ortel"')
    s.add_argument("datasets", nargs="*", help="dataset ids (default: all)")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    return {"record": cmd_record, "status": cmd_status, "verify": cmd_verify, "sign": cmd_sign}[a.cmd](a)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Dataset attestations

One signing record per dataset in `datasets/<id>.txt`, written by
`uv run scripts/attest_datasets.py record`. A record lists the BLAKE3 of every
committed file in the dataset's corpus folder and of every script that builds
it, plus what a signature attests. It holds no clock and no commit id, so it
changes exactly when the files do.

Signatures are OpenSSH Ed25519 (`ssh-keygen -Y`), in the namespace
`anthropic-pbc-dataset`, which is separate from the paper's `contrapunctus`
namespace (`docs/contrapunctus-attest.md`). A dataset signature cannot be
replayed as an endorsement of the paper.

## Sign

    uv run scripts/attest_datasets.py record        # then commit the records
    uv run scripts/attest_datasets.py sign --key ~/.ssh/YOUR_KEY --signer "Your Name" [dataset ...]

`sign` refuses a record that is not current. It runs each dataset's own
`verify` first and stops if that fails. `ssh-keygen` reads the key itself, from
the file or from the agent. The signer's public key is added once to
`allowed_signers`. Commit the `.sig`, the `.signer` file and `allowed_signers`.

## Check

    uv run scripts/attest_datasets.py status    # signed / unsigned / stale per dataset
    uv run scripts/attest_datasets.py verify    # exit 1 on a stale or bad signature

A signature goes **stale** when any listed file changes. The dataset is then
unsigned in effect until someone re-signs the new record. `DATASETS.md` shows
each dataset's status.

To bind a key to a person or organization, publish the same public key
somewhere they control, as the paper's protocol asks.

Signing is set up and committed (`4810456`, plus a one-line help-text fix in `38e337f`). Nothing is signed yet: that step needs your key.

**What the script does:**
- **Records:** `scripts/attest_datasets.py` writes one record per dataset into `attestations/datasets/`: the hash of every committed file and build script, and a short statement of what your signature means. It contains no date and no commit ID, so it changes exactly when the files change.
- **What your signature claims:** the files matched these hashes, the dataset's own `verify` passed, and the files came from the listed scripts run on the pinned sources. It does not vouch for any finding or any model output.
- **How it signs:** the same SSH method as the paper's protocol, but under its own label (`anthropic-pbc-dataset`), so a dataset signature can never pass as an endorsement of the paper.
- **Before signing:** it runs each dataset's `verify` and refuses to sign if that fails or if the record is out of date.
- **After any file change:** the signature shows as stale in `DATASETS.md` until you re-sign.

I tested the whole cycle with a throwaway key: it signed, verified, and flipped to stale after an edit. The test key and its signature are deleted, and nothing signed is committed.

**To sign everything,** run this at the prompt, with the `!` so the passphrase prompt comes to you. I'm assuming `id_ed25519`, but use whichever key you want tied to this; the name is how it will appear publicly.

```
! cd ~/dev/anthropic-pbc && uv run scripts/attest_datasets.py sign --key ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 --signer "YOUR NAME"
```

It runs every dataset's `verify` first, and the earnings-call one takes a few minutes. Afterwards I'll commit the signatures and `attestations/allowed_signers`. To tie the key to you, publish the same public key somewhere you control, for example on ethicic.com.

# Compute graph of every dataset step in this repository.
#
# Modelled on Our World in Data's ETL
# (https://docs.owid.io/projects/etl/architecture/design/compute-graph/): each
# step is a node named by a URI, and an edge means "depends on". When a node
# changes, every node downstream of it is stale. `uv run scripts/dag.py status`
# computes that from content hashes; nothing here reads a clock.
#
# URIs follow OWID's convention:

content.text:
The repo now follows OWID's compute-graph design. It's committed as `e83412f`, and every file stays where it was.

**What lines up with OWID:**
- **Step names.** Every dataset step has an OWID-style address: `snapshot://namespace/version/name` for upstream copies, and `data://channel/namespace/version/name` for built data. For example:
  - `snapshot://open_index/2026-08-31/hacker_news`
  - `data://meadow/earnings_calls/2026-11-04/ai_questions`
- **Channels.** Meadow is the verbatim extraction, and garden is deterministic counts and joins. I added one channel OWID doesn't have, `witness`, for model output. That builds the "a model's output is a proposal, not a finding" rule into the graph itself: anything reading witness output is visibly downstream of a model.
- **The graph.** `dag.yml` lists 26 steps, each with its build command, dependencies and outputs. It covers the earnings calls, Hacker News, Wikipedia, CVE, Epoch and the codebooks.
- **What needs rebuilding.** As in OWID, a change anywhere marks everything downstream as stale. Here it's detected from file contents, not timestamps. `scripts/dag.py` does four things:
  - `check`: confirms the graph has no cycles and every script and output exists
  - `lock`: records the current state in `dag.lock.tsv`

# Plan: regroup by the compute graph, with strict metadata

Status: PLAN · 2026-11-04. Requested by Sloane: regroup the repository along
OWID's ETL design (https://docs.owid.io/projects/etl/architecture/design/compute-graph/)
and be "ultra, ultra rigorous" about metadata.

## Goal

1. Every step in `dag.yml` lives at a path derived from its URI.
2. Every step carries complete metadata, and a missing field fails the build.

A reader holding any file can tell, from the file alone, what it is, where it
came from, how it was made, what each column means, and under what license.

## 1. Layout

OWID derives paths from URIs. We do the same:

| URI | Committed path | Bulk bytes (gitignored) |
|---|---|---|
| `snapshot://ns/version/name` | `snapshots/ns/version/name.meta.yml` and the MANIFEST | `.snapshots/ns/version/name/` |
| `data://meadow/ns/version/name` | `data/meadow/ns/version/name/` | `.data/meadow/...` for local-only text |
| `data://garden/ns/version/name` | `data/garden/ns/version/name/` | |
| `data://witness/ns/version/name` | `data/witness/ns/version/name/` (was `proposals/`) | shards |
| `data://gold/ns/version/name` | `data/gold/ns/version/name/` (was `gold/`) | |

`gold` is a new channel: human labels. It is never written by a model.

What changes:
- `corpus/`, `proposals/` and `gold/` are replaced.
- The dot-directories (`.eccorpus/`, `.hncorpus/`, ...) collapse into
  `.snapshots/` and `.data/`.

What stays:
- Scripts stay in `scripts/` and are named by `cmd` in each step. Splitting
  them per step, as OWID's `etl/steps/` does, can come later; it buys little
  while one script builds several steps.
- `docs/` stays as it is.
- The paper, `index.html`, and the seal and its hash pins are untouched; none
  of them reference these paths.

A compatibility note in each old folder's README points to the new path for
one release.

## 2. Metadata: required fields, enforced

The schema follows OWID's metadata reference (origin → dataset → table →
indicator) and adds fields this repository needs: hashes, witness status, and
what a dataset does not answer.

**Snapshot origin** (`<name>.meta.yml`). Every field is required, or `null`
with a `reason:`.
- `producer`, `title`, `description`
- `citation_full`, `attribution_short`
- `url_main`, `url_download`
- `date_published`, `date_accessed`, `version_producer`
- `license: {name, url}`, `terms_notes`: for example, YouGov's no-AI-ingestion
  notice, or third-party benchmark tables that keep their own licences
- `files`: path, bytes, SHA-256, BLAKE3. This absorbs the MANIFEST.
- `refetch`: `exact` | `saved_bytes_are_pin`, with the reason
- `personal_data`: `none` | `ids_only` | `verbatim_public_figures` | ...

**Dataset** (`<name>.meta.yml` beside the outputs):
- `title`, `description`, `channel`, `uri`
- `origins`: the snapshot URIs, resolved transitively
- `processing`: what the step does, in plain sentences, and what it drops
- `unit_of_analysis`, `denominator`: which file holds it
- `coverage`: dates, universe, known gaps
- `does_not_answer`: required; it may not be empty
- `license`: derived from the origins, the most restrictive wins
- `status`: held | witness | gold
- for `witness`: `model`, `revision`, `codebook`, and `proposal_only: true`

**Table** (one entry per output file):
- `title`, `description`, `primary_key`, `rows`
- `columns`, one entry for **every** column:
  - `title`, `description`, `type`, `unit`
  - for verbatim text: `verbatim: true`
  - for a hash column: `hash_of`
  - for a code column: `values`

**Enforcement** (`uv run scripts/dag.py check`). It fails when:
- a required field is missing or empty;
- a column in the file is not documented, or a documented column is not in the
  file;
- a hash in the metadata does not match the file;
- a `witness` dataset lacks `proposal_only: true`, or a non-witness step depends
  on a witness step without being marked a proposal;
- a license is weaker than an origin's.

Row counts and hashes are written by the build, never by hand. Descriptions
are written by hand and reviewed like code.

`DATASETS.md` renders all of this, so the deck becomes the human view of the
metadata.

## 3. Phases (one commit each, each verified)

1. **Schema and validator.** Write `schema/metadata.schema.yml`. Add checks to
   `dag.py check` that report missing metadata without failing yet, so we can
   see the gap.
2. **Metadata backfill.** One dataset per commit, starting with CVE and Epoch
   (smallest), then Wikipedia, Hacker News and the earnings calls. Columns are
   introspected from the files; descriptions are written and checked against
   the method docs.
3. **Regroup.** Wait until the v0.2 scoring and the democracy work have landed.
   Then `git mv` everything to the URI paths, in one commit per dataset:
   - update script constants and the graph's outputs;
   - rebuild, check byte-identical, `verify`, `dag.py lock`, re-record the
     attestations.
4. **Strict.** Flip `check` to fail on any gap, and add it to the
   collaboration rules in AGENTS.md.
5. **Signing.** Sloane signs once the layout is final. Signatures taken before
   the regroup would go stale on the move.

## Open decisions (also in OPENQUESTIONS.md)

- Whether `snapshots/` keeps a TSV MANIFEST beside the YAML for grep-ability
  (proposed: yes, generated from the YAML).
- Whether scripts split into per-step files now or later (proposed: later).

# CVE series: method
Data: [`corpus/cve/`](../corpus/cve/README.md). Code: `scripts/cve_series.py`.
## What it measures
The number of CVE records published each month since January 2020, how severe
their CNAs and ADPs scored them, which CNAs published them, and which ones
concern AI software or credit an AI system or AI lab. It rebuilds Epoch AI's CVE
explorer (https://epoch.ai/data/cve, CC BY 4.0) from the primary source, so the
same counts carry a pin, a hash and a rebuild command.
## Source and pin
`CVEProject/cvelistV5`, daily baseline release asset
`2026-11-04_all_CVEs_at_midnight.zip.zip` (every record as of 2026-11-04T00:00Z),
taken from release `cve_2026-11-04_0100Z`, the first release that carries it
(tag commit `dc7ec785f05ef024090048b6468bc7eddf06bc95`). Bytes, SHA-256 (equal to
GitHub's asset digest) and BLAKE3 are in `corpus/cve/MANIFEST.tsv`, as is the
inner `cves.zip` the build reads. The snapshot holds 418,964 records: 400,091
PUBLISHED, 18,873 REJECTED.
## Rules
| Step | Rule |
|---|---|
| State | `cveMetadata.state == "PUBLISHED"`. REJECTED records are dropped. |
| Universe | CVE id year ≥ 2020. This is what Epoch's "every published record 2020+" means in practice: its monthly totals equal ours only under the id-year rule. A CVE-2019-* id published in 2023 is outside. `n_published_any_id_year` shows the excluded mass (6,836 records in the window). |
| Month | `cveMetadata.datePublished[:7]`, UTC. Publication date, not discovery or reservation. 2020-01 through 2026-10, the last full month before the snapshot. |
| Severity | First CVSS base score found: CNA container first, then each ADP container in record order (in practice CISA's). Within a container, v4.0, then v3.1, then v3.0; v2 is ignored. Bucket by score: none 0, low 0.1–3.9, medium 4–6.9, high 7–8.9, critical 9–10; no score → unknown. |
| CNA | `cveMetadata.assignerShortName`, grouped into Epoch's 21 notable CNAs (mapping in `NOTABLE` in the script) or Other. Google = Chrome, ChromeOS, Google, GoogleCloud, Google_Devices, google_android. Samsung = Samsung Mobile, SamsungMobile, samsung.tv_appliance. GitHub = GitHub_P (own products), not GitHub_M (maintainer advisories, ~22,000 records). Red Hat excludes redhat-cnalr; VMware excludes brocade. |
| AI product (a) | `ANY_RE` from `scripts/ec_extract.py` (families ai, ai_phrase, ml, llm, vendor, agentic), plus the AI-software families in `AI_PRODUCT`: LangChain, LlamaIndex, Ollama, vLLM, MCP / Model Context Protocol, Hugging Face, PyTorch/TorchServe, TensorFlow/Keras, ONNX Runtime, llama.cpp/GGUF, chat front ends (Open WebUI, text-generation-webui, LibreChat, LobeChat, AnythingLLM, LoLLMs, LocalAI), ComfyUI/Stable Diffusion, Gradio, MLflow/Kubeflow/BentoML, LiteLLM, agent builders (Langflow, Flowise, Dify, AutoGPT, CrewAI, AutoGen, Semantic Kernel), NVIDIA AI (Triton Inference Server, TensorRT, DeepSpeed, NeMo), AI IDEs (Codeium, Windsurf, Anysphere). Searched in the CNA container's affected `vendor`, `product`, `packageName`, `repo` (field `product`) and English `descriptions` (field `description`). A bare `mcp` token counts in product fields only. |
| AI credit (b) | The CNA container's `credits[].value` only, never the description. Named systems in `AI_CREDIT`: Claude, Mythos, Anthropic, OpenAI, GPT/ChatGPT, Codex, Aardvark, Big Sleep/Naptime, DeepMind/CodeMender, Gemini, XBOW, Copilot, AIxCC/Team Atlanta, ZeroPath, Vulnhuntr. A credit naming none of them but carrying a generic AI term (ec_extract families ai, ai_phrase, ml, llm, agentic) is `ai_term`. "Claude" followed by a capitalised word counts only when that word is Code, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, Fable, Mythos, AI, Agent(s) or Security, so people named Claude are excluded. Each match keeps the credit's `type` (finder, reporter, tool, analyst, remediation developer, …; missing → `unspecified`). |
`n_ai_credited` counts records with any AI credit. `n_ai_credited_discovery`
drops records whose only AI credits are remediation types (remediation
developer, reviewer or verifier): a model that wrote the fix did not find the
bug. Per-system columns count records, so one record can count under Claude and
Anthropic both.
## Cross-check against Epoch
Epoch's page bundle (`https://epoch.ai/_astro/CveExplorerViz.D0wyPE-d.js`,
SHA-256 `ed04092a3ea8a7e06fedfd82e4db53c568fbd3a0ba4733c1e4c69a94f7553609`,
fetched 2026-11-04) embeds its monthly table as CSV (`month, cna, severity,
count`). Compared with `monthly.tsv` and `monthly-by-cna.tsv` for all 82 months
2020-01 to 2026-10:
- Monthly totals: 82 of 82 equal.
- Month × CNA (22 groups): every cell equal.
- Severity: critical, high, medium and unknown equal in every month. Epoch has
  no "none" bucket; its low equals our low + none. 112 records score 0.0.
- Epoch's partial 2026-11 count (1,356) equals the count of records in this
  snapshot published 2026-11-01..03, so Epoch's build used the same or an
  equivalent snapshot.
The AI columns have no Epoch counterpart.
## Selected values
| Month | Published | Linux CNA | Excl. Linux | AI product | AI credited | of which Claude | Anthropic | OpenAI | Codex |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2025-10 | 4,235 | 651 | 3,584 | 76 | 15 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 2026-04 | 5,650 | 377 | 5,273 | 280 | 29 | 14 | 17 | 1 | 1 |
| 2026-10 | 17,013 | 1,051 | 15,962 | 595 | 258 | 134 | 49 | 58 | 36 |
## What it does not answer
- **A CVE count measures reporting, not risk.** It counts records that a CNA
  chose to publish. It says nothing about exploitation, exposure, or harm.
- **The count moves when the reporting system moves.** CNA onboarding raises
  counts with no change in software: the Linux kernel became a CNA in February
  2024 and publishes thousands of fix-level records a year, which is why
  `n_excl_linux` exists. New CNAs, CNA backlogs and policy changes do the same.
- **AI-assisted discovery raises counts too.** The 2026 rise coincides with AI
  vulnerability-finding programmes (Epoch marks the Claude Mythos Preview
  announcement on 2026-04-07). This series can show the coincidence; it cannot
  separate more bugs found from more bugs reported, or AI's share from other
  causes.
- **AI credit is self-reported by CNAs and incomplete.** Credits are optional
  free text; many CNAs omit them, and an AI tool used by a human finder is often
  not named. A named lab (`anthropic`, `openai`) can mean a person employed
  there, not a model. `ai_term` is a loose residual that includes company names
  containing "AI" and the occasional personal name.
- **The product rule is a regex.** `description:vendor` and `description:ai`
  catch some non-AI records (a person named Claude in a kernel changelog, a

content.text:
Yes, it's the right time to regroup, before more data lands on the current layout. The plan, the schema and a working validator are in, and the first dataset passes it.

**The plan** is in `docs/plan-owid-regroup.md` (`2b8c78e`):
- **New layout:** every step moves to a folder named after its step address (`snapshots/…`, `data/meadow/…`, `data/garden/…`, `data/witness/…`), replacing `corpus/`, `proposals/` and `gold/`. Human labels become a new `data/gold` channel that a model never writes to.
- **Metadata:** we adopt OWID's four levels (where the data came from, the dataset, each table, each column) and add what we need on top:
  - hashes
  - whether something is model output
  - what each dataset does *not* answer, which can't be left empty
  - the terms of use, and whether a source contains personal data
- **Strictness:** a new check fails the build when a required field is missing or empty, when a file has a column the metadata doesn't describe (or the metadata describes one the file lacks), when a hash doesn't match, or when something downstream of model output isn't marked as a proposal.
- **Order of work:**
  1. schema and validator
  2. fill in the metadata, one dataset per commit
  3. move the files (after the current scoring and democracy jobs finish)
  4. make the check strict
  5. sign

  Signing comes last, because signatures taken before the move would go stale.

**Done so far:**
- **Schema:** `schema/metadata.schema.yml`.
- **Validator:** `uv run scripts/dag.py meta` reads the real columns from each file and lists every gap. For now it reports without failing.
- **First dataset:** CVE is complete, every column of its four tables described (`ef04fa8`).
- **"Unknown" stays visible:** a field can be marked unknown only with a stated reason, and those fields are counted and shown, never treated as done (`edda31f`).

Coverage is 2 of 26 steps.

**In progress:** three agents are filling in metadata in parallel, for the earnings calls (13 steps), HN plus Wikipedia (9) and Epoch (2 steps, 68 tables). Each has the same rule: every description must trace to the code, a method doc or the source's own documentation, and anything that can't be established gets marked unknown with a reason, never guessed. They'll also report anywhere the code contradicts the docs. The v0.2 scoring and the democracy agent are still running too.

Two small decisions are logged as Q12 in `OPENQUESTIONS.md`:
- keep a plain-table manifest next to each metadata file so it's easy to grep (I'd say yes)
- split scripts into one file per step now or later (I'd say later)

#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.10"
# dependencies = ["duckdb==2.0.0"]
# ///
"""The dialogue space under codebook-v0.2-draft: which sources discuss which AI risks.

For each source, the share of its AI-risk units (both witnesses >= 0.5 on
`ai_risk`) that also carry each risk type (both witnesses >= 0.5). Sources:
  executives   earnings-call windows not spoken by an analyst or the operator, 12 months to 2026-11-04
  analysts     analyst questions on calls, 12 months to 2026-11-04
  hn_anthropic Hacker News Anthropic/Claude windows, 2025-09..2026-08
  hn_security  Hacker News AI-security windows, 2025-09..2026-08
  wikipedia    Wikipedia AI-risk article windows, revisions as of 2026-11-04
DRAFT codebook, witness proposals, no gold set. Writes
proposals/cross-source/codebook-v0.2-draft/report/.

    uv run scripts/v02_map.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import sys
from html import escape
from pathlib import Path

import duckdb

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
CB = ROOT / "corpus" / "codebooks" / "codebook-v0.2-draft.tsv"
OUT = ROOT / "proposals" / "cross-source" / "codebook-v0.2-draft" / "report"
EC, HN, WP = ROOT / "corpus" / "earnings-calls", ROOT / "corpus" / "hacker-news", ROOT / "corpus" / "wikipedia-ai-risk"
P = ROOT / "proposals"
SOURCES = [  # (key, label, scores dir, id col, unit filter SQL over table u)
    ("executives", "Executives (calls)", P / "earnings-calls/codebook-v0.2-draft", "window_id",
     f"SELECT window_id AS id FROM '{EC / 'ai-windows.parquet'}' WHERE role NOT IN ('analyst_heuristic', 'operator') "
     "AND report_date::DATE > DATE '2025-11-04' AND report_date::DATE <= DATE '2026-11-04'"),
    ("analysts", "Analyst questions", P / "earnings-calls/codebook-v0.2-draft-questions", "question_id",
     f"SELECT question_id AS id FROM '{EC / 'ai-questions.parquet'}' "
     "WHERE report_date::DATE > DATE '2025-11-04' AND report_date::DATE <= DATE '2026-11-04'"),
    ("hn_anthropic", "HN: Anthropic", P / "hacker-news/anthropic-v0.2-draft", "window_id",
     f"""SELECT window_id AS id FROM '{HN / 'windows.parquet'}' WHERE "set" = 'anthropic' AND day BETWEEN '2025-09-01' AND '2026-08-31'"""),
    ("hn_security", "HN: AI security", P / "hacker-news/ai_security-v0.2-draft", "window_id",
     f"""SELECT window_id AS id FROM '{HN / 'windows.parquet'}' WHERE "set" = 'ai_security' AND day BETWEEN '2025-09-01' AND '2026-08-31'"""),
    ("wikipedia", "Wikipedia", P / "wikipedia-ai-risk/codebook-v0.2-draft", "window_id",
     f"SELECT window_id AS id FROM '{WP / 'windows.parquet'}'"),
]


def main() -> int:
    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    cb = list(csv.DictReader(CB.open(), delimiter="\t"))
    types = [r for r in cb if r["group"] == "risk_type"]
    con = duckdb.connect()
    shares: dict[str, dict[str, tuple[int, int]]] = {}
    for key, _, d, idc, units in SOURCES:
        con.execute(f"""CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE f AS
            SELECT x.{idc} AS id, x.hypothesis_id AS h, x.p_entail >= .5 AND y.p_entail >= .5 AS b
            FROM '{d / 'deberta.parquet'}' x JOIN '{d / 'modernbert.parquet'}' y USING ({idc}, hypothesis_id)
            WHERE x.{idc} IN ({units})""")
        risk = con.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM f WHERE h = 'ai_risk' AND b").fetchone()[0]
        shares[key] = {}
        for t in types:
            n = con.execute(f"""SELECT count(*) FROM f a JOIN f r USING (id)
                WHERE a.h = '{t['id']}' AND a.b AND r.h = 'ai_risk' AND r.b""").fetchone()[0]
            shares[key][t["id"]] = (n, risk)
    new = {r["id"] for r in cb if r["status"].startswith("v0.2")}
    rows = sorted(types, key=lambda t: -max(shares[k][t["id"]][0] / max(shares[k][t["id"]][1], 1) for k, *_ in SOURCES))
    with (OUT / "dialogue-space.tsv").open("w") as f:
        f.write("# Share (%) of each source's AI-risk units naming each risk type; both witnesses >= 0.5. "
                "codebook-v0.2-draft (DRAFT wording), witness proposals, no gold set.\n")
        f.write("risk_type\tnew_in_v0.2\t" + "\t".join(f"{k}_pct\t{k}_n" for k, *_ in SOURCES) + "\n")
        f.write("ai_risk_units\t\t" + "\t".join(f"\t{shares[k][types[0]['id']][1]}" for k, *_ in SOURCES) + "\n")
        for t in rows:
            cells = []
            for k, *_ in SOURCES:
                n, base = shares[k][t["id"]]
                cells += [f"{100 * n / base:.1f}" if base else "", str(n)]
            f.write(f"{t['id']}\t{'yes' if t['id'] in new else ''}\t" + "\t".join(cells) + "\n")
    plot(rows, shares, new)
    print(f"wrote {OUT.relative_to(ROOT)}/dialogue-space.tsv and .svg")
    return 0


def plot(rows, shares, new) -> None:
    """Heatmap: risk types x sources, cell = share; one sequential hue, value printed."""
    cw, rh, left, top = 128, 24, 210, 96
    W, H = left + cw * len(SOURCES) + 24, top + rh * len(rows) + 64
    def fill(v: float) -> str:  # light -> dark blue, sequential
        t = min(v / 50.0, 1.0)
        lo, hi = (236, 243, 249), (16, 70, 120)
        return "#%02x%02x%02x" % tuple(round(a + (b - a) * t) for a, b in zip(lo, hi))
    o = [f'<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 {W} {H}" font-family="system-ui,-apple-system,sans-serif" role="img">',
         '<style>text{fill:#1b1b1b}.m{fill:#5f6368}</style>', f'<rect width="{W}" height="{H}" fill="#fcfcfb"/>',
         '<text x="16" y="30" font-size="18" font-weight="600">Who talks about which AI risks</text>',
         '<text x="16" y="52" font-size="12" class="m">Share of each source\'s AI-risk passages naming each type. '
         'Codebook v0.2 DRAFT; * = new in v0.2.</text>']
    for j, (_, label, *_r) in enumerate(SOURCES):
        o.append(f'<text x="{left + j * cw + cw / 2}" y="{top - 10}" font-size="12" font-weight="600" text-anchor="middle">{escape(label)}</text>')
    for i, t in enumerate(rows):
        y = top + i * rh
        o.append(f'<text x="{left - 8}" y="{y + rh / 2 + 4}" font-size="12" text-anchor="end">{escape(t["id"])}{" *" if t["id"] in new else ""}</text>')
        for j, (k, label, *_r) in enumerate(SOURCES):
            n, base = shares[k][t["id"]]
            v = 100 * n / base if base else 0.0
            ink = "#ffffff" if v >= 25 else "#1b1b1b"
            o.append(f'<g><title>{escape(label)}: {escape(t["id"])} {v:.1f}% ({n} of {base})</title>'
                     f'<rect x="{left + j * cw + 1}" y="{y + 1}" width="{cw - 2}" height="{rh - 2}" rx="2" fill="{fill(v)}"/>'
                     f'<text x="{left + j * cw + cw / 2}" y="{y + rh / 2 + 4}" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle" style="fill:{ink}">{v:.0f}</text></g>')
    o.append(f'<text x="16" y="{H - 16}" font-size="11" class="m">Both NLI witnesses ≥ 0.5 on ai_risk and on the type; a unit can name several. '
             'Calls and questions: 12 months to 2026-11-04; HN: 2025-09..2026-08; Wikipedia: revisions as of 2026-11-04.</text>')
    o.append("</svg>")
    (OUT / "dialogue-space.svg").write_text("\n".join(o) + "\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

cat >> docs/bert-enrichment-spec.md <<'EOF'

### 2026-11-04 · Codebook v0.2 DRAFT across five sources; batch-dependence of bf16 scores

**Status: witness proposals on a draft codebook; no gold set; wording awaits
review (OPENQUESTIONS Q2).**

- **Codebook.** `corpus/codebooks/codebook-v0.2-draft.tsv` keeps the 16 v0.1
  hypotheses word for word and adds 14. Each new one cites the Wikipedia
  heading and revision it came from.
- **Sources scored.** Earnings-call windows, analyst questions, both HN sets,
  and the Wikipedia windows. Both witnesses ran on Modal L40S in bf16.
- **Reproducibility finding.** Re-scoring the unchanged v0.1 hypotheses
  inside the larger codebook did *not* reproduce the v0.1 scores, though the
  model, GPU type, text and hypothesis were all the same.

  | Run | Max \|Δp\| | Calls flipped at 0.5 |
  |---|---|---|
  | Calls, DeBERTa | 0.13 | 244 of 617,600 (0.04%) |
  | Calls, ModernBERT | 0.05 | 1 |
  | HN, DeBERTa | 0.19 | 936 of 1,688,944 (0.06%) |
  | HN, ModernBERT | 0.26 | 292 |

  The likely cause is bf16 arithmetic varying with batch composition: a
  30-hypothesis codebook groups pairs differently than a 16-hypothesis one.
  So bf16 scores are reproducible only for the same codebook, batch and
  hardware. They are not invariant to batch composition. That is a narrower
  claim than the spec's §5 Route B, which already declines to claim
  reproducibility across hardware. Rates built on these scores move by about
  0.05% of decisions. A float32 rerun would show whether precision is the

**Who talks about which AI risks.** Each figure is the share of that source's AI-risk passages that mention the risk.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AI-risk passages (n) | 179 | 64 | 6,281 | 3,096 | 833 |
| Cyber | 40% | 20% | 23% | 85% | 19% |

- **Executives and analysts talk about a narrow band:** cyber, capex and disruption. Almost every new dimension is at zero for them.
- **Wikipedia covers the widest range.** Hacker News falls in between and leans toward transparency and loss of control.
- **The call samples are small.** The executive and analyst columns rest on 179 and 64 passages, so their single-digit percentages can be a handful of passages.

**Two problems I found:**
1. **The bio/chem hypothesis doesn't work.** On Wikipedia's own "Biosecurity" section it scores about 0.001. My wording ("helping to create biological or chemical weapons") is narrower than how the topic is actually written about. It needs rewording as part of your review, and we can't say anything about bio risk until then.
2. **The model scores aren't exactly reproducible.** Rescoring the 16 unchanged hypotheses inside the bigger codebook didn't give identical scores: the same model, GPU type and text moved by up to 0.26, and about 0.05% of yes/no calls flipped. The likely cause is that reduced-precision arithmetic (bf16) varies with how pairs are batched. That's a narrower guarantee than I had assumed, and it's logged in the spec. A full-precision rerun would show whether precision is the whole cause; it costs a few dollars on any GPU.

- **`a00fd5e`** adds the metadata for the three democracy steps. Nine fields are left empty, each with a stated reason:

- **`80f27a1`** fixes seven places where the democracy code or docs disagreed with the data. I checked each against the files first:
  - The script and README called the Rooney numbers "stated conditions"; they are stated attitudes, which is what the method doc's limits section says.
  - The scraper's user agent called the folder CC0 public domain; its README says it is not.
  - "Each report is two pages around one to three charts" was wrong: R01 has one page, and R06 and R10 each have a page with no images.

  - The build checks each quote against its PDF page and each number against its quote. It does not check the hand-entered wave, group, item or response columns, and the response label isn't a word of the quote in 56 of 129 rows. The doc and the compute graph now both say so.

# Praxis

Praxis is the governing layer for Ethical Capital's open-source modules. It
states why the work matters, who governs it, and the rules every module
inherits. It holds no code.

**License:** being researched (G2). Until one is chosen, nothing here is
licensed for reuse.

**Status: a draft for public review.** Expect it to be wrong in places.
Criticism is the input this draft exists to collect, and a revision stands
against the text it replaces instead of erasing it (P12). Only the safety
gates G2 and G5 to G9 block publication. Rough or unfinished material does
not.

**Objective.** Build a public epistemic commons: what is true, what is fair
and what is public about the companies and institutions we research. Every
statement in it can be checked from the bytes, and anyone affected by a
statement can contest it.

**Method.** Praxis defines one chain of modules. Each module consumes only
what the module before it produced and verified:

| Module | Answers | Produces | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Descartes** | What is true? | content-addressed claims, each quoting its evidence byte for byte, re-verified from scratch on every run | built; its loop passes on darwin-arm64 |
| **Rawls** | What is fair? | evaluations of claims under named frameworks, made behind a veil of ignorance: the reasoning is judged without knowing whose interest it serves, and it covers the conduct that law does not constrain | designed (`descartes/docs/primitives.md`: evaluation, framework, `against`, `interest`); not built |
| **Arendt** | What is public? | exports of the graph and its evaluations, and contests by the people and companies named in them, resolved through open discernment rather than administrative decree | not designed |

**Name (G1, decided 2026-11-03).** Praxis is the open-source brand. The
monocloud glossary (`monocloud/docs/praxis/CONTEXT.md`) still says Praxis is
"not a public brand" and calls the open layer the "Data Commons". It has to
be updated to match (work order item 1).

## 0. The template standard

This section is the canonical copy. Every module's README has these sections,
in this order. A section with nothing in it yet still appears, with the line
`none yet`.

| § | Section | What it must state |
|---|---|---|
| — | Header | name; "part of Praxis"; license; objective in one sentence; method in three |
| 0 | Template standard | which version of this table the module follows (G4) |
| 1 | Run it | the exact commands, and what a plain run versus an accepting run does |
| 2 | Constraints | the inherited rules (this file's §2), plus the module's own, each naming its check or marked **open** |
| 3 | The machine | pseudocode for every operation the code performs |
| 4 | Data | every stored format, with exact keys or columns |
| 5 | The loop | each step's guarantee and what it compares against, plus the assumption register |
| 6 | Supply chain and isolation | dependencies with their governance, build isolation, network steps |
| 7 | Signing | keys, what gets signed, and where signatures live |
| 8 | Inputs | how outside material becomes data the module trusts |
| 9 | Contracts | the table: contract, enforced by, proved by, status |
| 10 | Work order | open contracts, ordered by what blocks a passing loop |
| 11 | Not part of this module | design notes, records, and what is out of scope |

Status values in every contracts table:
- **held**: code blocks the break, and a test proves it;
- **code-only**: code blocks it, but nothing proves it;
- **partial**: some of the break is blocked;
- **open**: stated, not enforced;
- **decide**: the rule itself needs a decision.

#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.10"
# dependencies = ["blake3==1.0.11", "pyyaml==6.0.2", "duckdb==2.0.0"]
# ///
"""The compute graph in dag.yml: check it, lock it, and find what is stale.

Modelled on OWID's ETL graph: a step is a node named by a URI, an edge means
"depends on", and a change anywhere makes everything downstream stale. Change
is read from content, never from a clock or file times:

  input hash   BLAKE3 over the step's scripts (from `cmd`), its extra `inputs`,
               and the output hash of every dependency
  output hash  BLAKE3 over (path, BLAKE3) of every file in `outputs`

dag.lock.tsv records both for every step at the last `lock`. `status` compares:

  ok        inputs and outputs match the lock
  rebuilt   outputs changed with the same inputs: downstream must refresh
  inputs    a script or an upstream output changed: rebuild this step
  upstream  something above it is not ok

    uv run scripts/dag.py check            # URIs, deps, cycles, outputs exist
    uv run scripts/dag.py status           # per step, in dependency order (exit 1 if any not ok)
    uv run scripts/dag.py plan [URI ...]   # rebuild commands for not-ok steps (or URI + descendants)
    uv run scripts/dag.py lock             # record current hashes, after a verified rebuild
    uv run scripts/dag.py mermaid          # the graph as a Mermaid flowchart
    uv run scripts/dag.py meta [--strict]  # metadata gaps against schema/metadata.schema.yml

A step names its metadata file with `meta:` (YAML). Columns are read from the
files themselves (parquet schema, TSV/CSV header), so every column must be
documented and every documented column must exist.
"""

#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.10"
# dependencies = ["blake3==1.0.11", "pyyaml==6.0.2"]
# ///
"""Write DATASETS.md, the central catalog of every corpus, as a Marp deck.

One registry, corpus/datasets.tsv, holds what cannot be read from files: title,
source, license, pin date, how often the source changes, and the refresh
commands. Everything else is read from the repository: each corpus's
MANIFEST.tsv (row count and BLAKE3), its committed files, and the witness runs
under proposals/<id>/. No clock: the deck changes only when the inputs change.

    uv run scripts/datasets_md.py          # write DATASETS.md
    uv run scripts/datasets_md.py check    # exit 1 if DATASETS.md is stale

Render: npx @marp-team/marp-cli DATASETS.md   (or the Marp VS Code extension)
"""

from __future__ import annotations
#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.10"
# dependencies = ["blake3==1.0.11"]
# ///
"""Signing records for each dataset, and SSH signatures over them.

The paper has its own attestation protocol (docs/contrapunctus-attest.md). This
is the same mechanism for the corpora: OpenSSH Ed25519 signatures
(`ssh-keygen -Y`), in a separate namespace, `anthropic-pbc-dataset`, so a
dataset signature can never be replayed as an endorsement of the paper.

A record lists, for one dataset in corpus/datasets.tsv:
  - the BLAKE3 of every committed file in its corpus folder;
  - the BLAKE3 of every script its refresh command runs;
  - what a signature over the record attests.
It holds no clock and no commit id, so it is a pure function of the files. When
any file changes, the record changes, and an old signature stops verifying: the
dataset shows as stale until someone re-signs.

    uv run scripts/attest_datasets.py record                 # write attestations/datasets/<id>.txt
    uv run scripts/attest_datasets.py sign --key ~/.ssh/KEY --signer "NAME"   # run by the signer
    uv run scripts/attest_datasets.py verify                 # exit 1 on a bad or stale signature
    uv run scripts/attest_datasets.py status                 # signed / unsigned / stale per dataset

`sign` runs `verify` for each dataset's own build first (`<script> verify`),
when the script has one, and refuses to sign a record that is not current.
"""

# Dataset attestations

One signing record per dataset in `datasets/<id>.txt`, written by
`uv run scripts/attest_datasets.py record`. A record lists the BLAKE3 of every
committed file in the dataset's corpus folder and of every script that builds
it, plus what a signature attests. It holds no clock and no commit id, so it
changes exactly when the files do.

Signatures are OpenSSH Ed25519 (`ssh-keygen -Y`), in the namespace
`anthropic-pbc-dataset`, which is separate from the paper's `contrapunctus`
namespace (`docs/contrapunctus-attest.md`). A dataset signature cannot be
replayed as an endorsement of the paper.

## Sign

    uv run scripts/attest_datasets.py record        # then commit the records
    uv run scripts/attest_datasets.py sign --key ~/.ssh/YOUR_KEY --signer "Your Name" [dataset ...]

`sign` refuses a record that is not current. It runs each dataset's own
`verify` first and stops if that fails. `ssh-keygen` reads the key itself, from
the file or from the agent. The signer's public key is added once to
`allowed_signers`. Commit the `.sig`, the `.signer` file and `allowed_signers`.

## Check

    uv run scripts/attest_datasets.py status    # signed / unsigned / stale per dataset
    uv run scripts/attest_datasets.py verify    # exit 1 on a stale or bad signature

A signature goes **stale** when any listed file changes. The dataset is then
unsigned in effect until someone re-signs the new record. `DATASETS.md` shows
each dataset's status.

To bind a key to a person or organization, publish the same public key
somewhere they control, as the paper's protocol asks.

- **`DATASETS.md`** is the catalog of every corpus: source, license, pin date,
  how often the source changes, refresh commands, and witness runs. It is a

  step has a URI: `snapshot://namespace/version/name` for an upstream copy, and
  `data://<meadow|garden|witness>/namespace/version/name` for a built dataset.
  `witness` is our own channel, for model output. `uv run scripts/dag.py status`

  the rebuild commands in order. Cite data in docs by step URI.
- **`OPENQUESTIONS.md`** holds decisions waiting on someone, with owner and
  context. Add one whenever your work hits a choice that isn't yours to make.

I moved all four groups to `~/dev/praxis` and removed them from anthropic-pbc. Run from anthropic-pbc, the moved tools give the same results as before: all 36 steps up to date, metadata complete with 0 gaps, and the catalog deck current.

**Now in Praxis:**
- `datasets/` holds the three tools (`dag.py`, `datasets_md.py`, `attest_datasets.py`), the metadata schema (`metadata.schema.yml`), the signing instructions (`signing.md`) and the regroup plan (`plan-owid-regroup.md`).
- `OPENQUESTIONS.md` and `PASTEBIN.md` are at the root.
- The tools now take the current directory as the repo they describe. You run them from the anthropic-pbc root, e.g. `uv run ../praxis/datasets/dag.py status`.

**Staying in anthropic-pbc**, because each describes this repo's own data: `dag.yml`, `dag.lock.tsv`, the 36 metadata files, `corpus/datasets.tsv`, the signing records in `attestations/datasets/`, and `DATASETS.md`. AGENTS.md now points to Praxis for the tools and notes. The metadata files' header comments name the schema's new location.

The commits are `309d25a` in anthropic-pbc and `8e309c6` in praxis. Praxis had 17 files staged by another session; I left them staged and uncommitted. My praxis commit first picked up Python cache files, so I amended it to drop them and added a `.gitignore` for them.

What this changes:
- **Strangers can't rebuild anthropic-pbc.** AGENTS.md promises that anyone can clone the repo and rebuild every dataset. Praxis has no git remote, and its README says nothing in it is licensed for reuse yet. Until Praxis is published, the graph checks, catalog and signing only work on your machine.
- **Praxis's README says it "holds no code".** It now holds three scripts.
- **The tools are still anthropic-pbc-specific.** `datasets_md.py` reads this repo's Epoch and `proposals/` folders, and the signing namespace is hard-coded as `anthropic-pbc-dataset`. Another repo can't use them as they stand.
- **The notes are about anthropic-pbc.** Most of Q1–Q14 concern this repo, but they now sit at Praxis's root.

Which of these to fix, and in what order, is your call. I haven't touched Praxis's README.

#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.13"
# dependencies = [
#   "matplotlib==3.10.7",
# ]
# ///
"""Charts for DECK.md that no corpus report draws yet. Reads committed tables only.

  deck/cve-ai-credit.svg     CVEs published per month, and CVEs whose CNA credits
                             name an AI system (Claude highlighted). corpus/cve/.
  deck/gdelt-attention.svg   Share of online news monitored by GDELT that says
                             "health of democracy", and that mentions Anthropic.
                             corpus/democracy/gdelt-timelines.tsv.

Two measures of different scale are drawn as two panels, never a dual axis.
Deterministic: fixed svg.hashsalt, no Date metadata.

    uv run scripts/deck_charts.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import sys
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
OUT = ROOT / "deck"
CVE = ROOT / "corpus" / "cve" / "monthly-ai.tsv"
GDELT = ROOT / "corpus" / "democracy" / "gdelt-timelines.tsv"

# Same palette as the corpus reports (dataviz reference palette, light mode).
SURFACE, INK, INK2, GRID = "#fcfcfb", "#0b0b0b", "#52514e", "#e4e3df"
S1, S2, MUTED = "#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#a8a69f"


def rows(p: Path) -> list[dict]:
    with p.open() as f:
        return list(csv.DictReader((l for l in f if not l.startswith("#")), delimiter="\t"))


def setup():
    import matplotlib
    matplotlib.use("svg")
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
    plt.rcParams.update({"svg.hashsalt": "deck", "font.family": "DejaVu Sans", "font.size": 10,
                         "axes.edgecolor": INK2, "axes.labelcolor": INK2, "xtick.color": INK2,
                         "ytick.color": INK2})
    return matplotlib, plt


def style(ax) -> None:
    ax.set_facecolor(SURFACE)
    ax.grid(axis="y", color=GRID, lw=0.8)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
    for s in ("top", "right", "left"):
        ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)
    ax.tick_params(length=0)


def cve(matplotlib, plt) -> None:
    r = [x for x in rows(CVE) if x["month"] >= "2023-01"]
    months = [x["month"] for x in r]
    xs = range(len(months))
    pub = [int(x["n_published"]) for x in r]
    ai = [int(x["n_ai_credited"]) for x in r]
    claude = [int(x["n_credit_claude"]) for x in r]
    other = [a - c for a, c in zip(ai, claude)]
    ticks = [i for i, m in enumerate(months) if m.endswith("-01")]
    labels = [months[i][:4] for i in ticks]

    fig, (a1, a2) = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(9, 6.2), facecolor=SURFACE, sharex=True,
                                 gridspec_kw={"hspace": 0.45})
    style(a1)
    a1.bar(xs, pub, color=S1, width=0.78)
    a1.annotate(f"{pub[-1]:,}", (xs[-1], pub[-1]), xytext=(0, 4), textcoords="offset points",
                ha="center", color=INK, fontsize=9, fontweight="bold")
    a1.yaxis.set_major_formatter(matplotlib.ticker.FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"{v:,.0f}"))
    a1.set_title("CVEs published per month", loc="left", color=INK, fontsize=11, fontweight="bold")

    style(a2)
    a2.bar(xs, claude, color=S2, width=0.78, label="Credit names Claude")
    a2.bar(xs, other, bottom=claude, color=MUTED, width=0.78, label="Credit names another AI system or term")
    a2.annotate(f"{ai[-1]} ({claude[-1]} Claude)", (xs[-1], ai[-1]), xytext=(-4, 4),
                textcoords="offset points", ha="right", color=INK, fontsize=9, fontweight="bold")
    a2.set_title("CVEs whose credits name an AI system, per month", loc="left", color=INK,
                 fontsize=11, fontweight="bold")
    a2.legend(loc="upper left", frameon=False, fontsize=9, labelcolor=INK)
    a2.set_xticks(ticks, labels)
    fig.suptitle("Vulnerability disclosures, and the share credited to AI", x=0.01, ha="left",
                 color=INK, fontsize=13, fontweight="bold")
    fig.text(0.01, 0.01, f"Source: CVEProject/cvelistV5 baseline 2026-11-04 (corpus/cve). Months "
             f"{months[0]} to {months[-1]}. Credit = CNA credits field only, matched to named systems; "
             "method credit Epoch AI (CC BY).", color=INK2, fontsize=7)
    fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.08, right=0.98, top=0.88, bottom=0.1)
    fig.savefig(OUT / "cve-ai-credit.svg", facecolor=SURFACE, metadata={"Date": None, "Creator": None})
    plt.close(fig)


def gdelt(matplotlib, plt) -> None:
    by: dict[str, dict[str, list[float]]] = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(list))
    for x in rows(GDELT):
        if x["source"] == "doc" and x["mode"] == "timelinevol" and x["query_id"] in ("hod", "anthropic"):
            by[x["query_id"]][x["date"][:6]].append(float(x["value"]))
    months = sorted(set(by["hod"]) | set(by["anthropic"]))
    months = [m for m in months if "201701" <= m <= "202610"]
    xs = range(len(months))
    ticks = [i for i, m in enumerate(months) if m.endswith("01")]
    labels = [months[i][:4] for i in ticks]

    def mean(q: str) -> list[float]:
        return [sum(by[q][m]) / len(by[q][m]) if by[q].get(m) else 0.0 for m in months]

    fig, (a1, a2) = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(9, 6.2), facecolor=SURFACE, sharex=True,
                                 gridspec_kw={"hspace": 0.45})
    for ax, q, color, title in ((a1, "hod", S1, '"Health of democracy"'), (a2, "anthropic", S2, "Anthropic")):
        style(ax)
        ys = mean(q)
        ax.plot(xs, ys, color=color, lw=2)
        pk = max(range(len(ys)), key=ys.__getitem__)
        ax.annotate(f"peak {months[pk][:4]}-{months[pk][4:]}", (pk, ys[pk]), xytext=(0, 5),
                    textcoords="offset points", ha="center", color=INK, fontsize=9)
        ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(matplotlib.ticker.FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"{v:.3f}%"))
        ax.set_ylim(0, None)
        ax.set_title(f"{title}: % of monitored online news articles (monthly mean of daily values)",
                     loc="left", color=INK, fontsize=10.5, fontweight="bold")
    a2.set_xticks(ticks, labels)
    fig.suptitle("News attention: the health of democracy, and Anthropic", x=0.01, ha="left",
                 color=INK, fontsize=13, fontweight="bold")
    fig.text(0.01, 0.01, "Source: GDELT DOC 2.0 API, timelinevol, responses saved 2026-11-04 "
             "(corpus/democracy). Attention, not effect: neither line measures anything Anthropic does "
             "to democracy.", color=INK2, fontsize=7)
    fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.09, right=0.98, top=0.88, bottom=0.1)
    fig.savefig(OUT / "gdelt-attention.svg", facecolor=SURFACE, metadata={"Date": None, "Creator": None})
    plt.close(fig)


def main() -> int:
    OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    matplotlib, plt = setup()
    cve(matplotlib, plt)
    gdelt(matplotlib, plt)
    print("wrote deck/cve-ai-credit.svg, deck/gdelt-attention.svg")
    return 0

1. **Anthropic's charter is legally real and legally toothless.** The public
   benefit purpose sits in its certificate and DGCL §362 requires balancing
   stockholders, "those materially affected," and that purpose. But §365(b)
   gives directors **no duty to any person on account of a public-benefit
   interest**, and §367 limits enforcement to derivative suits by holders of
   ≥2% (or $2M, lesser, once listed). The public the charter names cannot
   enforce it. **[CONFIRMED/HIGH]**
2. **The Report grades its own homework — and its own LTBT says so.** The
   Trust: the report "largely describes inputs; in subsequent reports we will
   increasingly look for Anthropic to produce outcomes" (p.17). Flagship
   benefit counts (33,000+ critical flaws; a 129,000 program-total that is
   **not in the PBC Report** — partner-reported, caught by the loop audit) have no public

   Claude*. **[UNVERIFIED counts; MISLEADING if read as verified]**
3. **Present, Anthropic-attributable harm is documented and priced; present,
   Anthropic-attributable benefit is mostly anecdote.** Priced: the $1.5B
   *Bartz* settlement over ~500,000 pirated books (~7M downloaded); an

   the stronger argument.** No study counts millions of individually verified

Paper: `docs/anthropic-contrapunctus.md`. Every chart here rebuilds from committed files. Model output in these charts comes from witnesses: two NLI models whose labels are proposals, not hand-verified findings. --- ## The argument in one line **Anthropic's charter is legally real and legally toothless.** - §365(b) gives directors no duty to any person on account of a public-benefit interest. - §367 limits enforcement to holders of ≥2% (or $2M, lesser, once listed). - The public the charter names cannot enforce it. The rest of this deck looks outward at what public data says about AI risk and Anthropic: - **S&P 500 earnings calls:** what companies and analysts say about AI. - **Hacker News:** what practitioners say about Anthropic and AI security. - **Wikipedia:** the map of AI-risk ideas. - **The CVE record:** what the vulnerability database credits to AI. --- ![w:900](proposals/earnings-calls/codebook-v0.1/report/ai-risk-by-year.svg)

Analysts ask how AI sells (21.2% of AI questions) far more than how it is governed (0.8%). This bears on App. E: almost nobody on a call asks about control.

# The report as a build product

Status: plan, 2026-11-04. Nothing below is built yet except the first deck
(`DECK.md`, hand-assembled).

## Principle

The paper is not edited; it is **built**. An edition is a deterministic function
of one source commit and a few recorded parameters:

    edition = build(source commit, codebook version)

Rerunning the build at the same commit with the same parameters gives the same
bytes. Building produces a **new commit** whose parent is the source commit, so
every edition names exactly the code, data, codebook and prose it came from.

`docs/anthropic-contrapunctus.md` at `1afb042` ("v0, finalized") is **edition
v0**. It was written by hand and stays frozen as it is. Editions from v1 on are
built.

## What goes in

1. **Data**: the steps in `dag.yml`. The build refuses to run unless
   `dag.py status` is all `ok`, so every table it reads is locked by hash.
2. **One codebook version** for every model-labelled chart and number in the
   edition. Mixing versions is a build error. This is the fix for the first
   deck, which shows v0.1 charts beside a v0.2-draft chart (executives'
   cybersecurity share reads 36% on one slide and 40% on another).
3. **Charts**: scripts that turn tables into SVG, with the codebook version
   as an argument and printed on the chart.
4. **Bindings**: every number in the prose is a reference to a table cell, a
   computed value, or a Descartes claim id (`docs/descartes-spec.md`). There
   are no hand-typed numbers; a lint fails the build on a bare figure in
   bound prose.
5. **Prose templates**: the argument, written and reviewed by people
   (buzz-saw and brand-voice passes apply to the templates).

## What comes out

An edition folder holding the rendered paper, the deck, the charts it used,
and a stamp file:

- source commit;
- codebook version;
- BLAKE3 of `dag.lock.tsv` (and of the Praxis catalog pin, once the data moves
  there);
- tool versions (Python packages, Marp CLI);
- the BLAKE3 of every output file.

A human signs the stamp (the dataset attestation mechanism, applied to the
edition). Agents never sign.

## Checks the build enforces

- every `dag.yml` step `ok`;
- one codebook version across all charts and bindings;
- every binding resolves; no unbound number in bound prose;
- a rebuild at the source commit is byte-identical.

## First target

`DECK.md` becomes edition output: `deck_charts.py` and the corpus report
charts take `--codebook`, slide captions take their numbers from bindings, and
the build writes the deck with its stamp. The paper template comes later.

## Open decisions

1. **Codebook for the first built edition**: v0.1 (reviewed; analysts'
   questions were never scored against it, so the cross-source chart loses
   them) or v0.2 (all five sources; every chart says DRAFT until its wording is
   approved, OPENQUESTIONS Q2).
2. **Where editions live**: a folder per edition in this repository, git tags
   with release assets, or both.
3. **Whether the build commits by itself** or leaves a tree for a person to
   review and commit.
4. **How bindings and Descartes claims meet**: whether every binding becomes a
   Descartes claim, or only quotes from outside documents do.
5. **Where the data lives** when this runs: here, or the Praxis catalog
   (paused, pending the other session's registry work).

78	        FROM m LEFT JOIN c ON strftime(c.day, '%Y-%m') = m.month GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1""").fetchall()

97	    with EC_RANK.open() as f:

99	    tot = int(re.search(r"\((\d+) windows\)", raw[0]).group(1))   # windows proposed ai_risk

107	        for st in SETS:

167	                     f'<text x="{x0 + bw + 4:.1f}" y="{y + rowh / 2 + 4}" font-size="11" class="m">{v:.0f}</text></g>')

#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.13"
# dependencies = [
#   "blake3==1.0.11",
#   "duckdb==2.0.0",
#   "matplotlib==3.10.7",
# ]
# ///
"""Build DECK.md as an edition of one source commit and one risk codebook.

    uv run scripts/build_edition.py --codebook v0.2-draft    # write DECK.md, deck/*.svg, deck/STAMP.json
    uv run scripts/build_edition.py --codebook v0.2-draft --check   # exit 1 if a rebuild would change anything

The build is the review step. It writes into the working tree and never
commits. Review `git diff`, then commit the edition yourself. The stamp names
the source commit (HEAD at build time), so the edition commit's parent is the
commit it was built from.

Rules (docs/report-build.md):
  - every dag.yml step must be `ok` (Praxis dag.py status);
  - every input the build reads must be committed and unmodified;
  - one risk codebook for every risk chart and number;
  - every number in the deck comes from a binding computed here; a digit in
    the template outside {{...}} on a caption line fails the build;
  - quotes from the paper are checked against edition v0 at PAPER_V0.
Positive = both witnesses (DeBERTa, ModernBERT) >= 0.5, everywhere.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import json
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import blake3
import duckdb

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "scripts"))
import deck_charts  # noqa: E402

TEMPLATE = ROOT / "deck" / "deck.template.md"
OUT_MD = ROOT / "DECK.md"
OUT_DIR = ROOT / "deck"
STAMP = OUT_DIR / "STAMP.json"
EC = ROOT / "corpus" / "earnings-calls"
PAPER = "docs/anthropic-contrapunctus.md"
PAPER_V0 = "1afb042"
DAG_TOOL = ROOT.parent / "praxis" / "datasets" / "dag.py"
FIRST_YEAR = 2013
RISK_WORD = r"(?i)\brisk(s|y|ier|iest)?\b"

# Risk codebooks this build supports: codebook file, score folder for earnings-call windows,
# the cross-source chart for that codebook, and a status shown on every slide.
CODEBOOKS = {
    "v0.2-draft": {
        "file": "corpus/codebooks/codebook-v0.2-draft.tsv",
        "ec_scores": "proposals/earnings-calls/codebook-v0.2-draft",
        "dialogue": "proposals/cross-source/codebook-v0.2-draft/report/dialogue-space.tsv",
        "status": " (DRAFT: wording awaits review)",
    },
}
# Fixed inputs read whatever the codebook (their own codebooks are recorded in the stamp).
FIXED = {
    "question_intents": "proposals/earnings-calls/codebook-questions-v0.1/report/ttm.tsv",
    "question_chart": "proposals/earnings-calls/codebook-questions-v0.1/report/intent-ttm.svg",
    "dialogue_chart": "proposals/cross-source/codebook-v0.2-draft/report/dialogue-space.svg",
    "cve_monthly_ai": "corpus/cve/monthly-ai.tsv",
}
LABELS = {"regulation": "Regulation", "cyber": "Cybersecurity", "privacy": "Data privacy",
          "accuracy": "Accuracy / hallucination", "bias": "Bias / fairness", "labor": "Jobs / labor",
          "disruption": "Disruption of the business", "capex": "Overspending / capex return",
          "energy": "Energy / power", "supply": "Chip & supply constraints", "ip": "Intellectual property",
          "safety_ethics": "Safety / ethics / misuse"}
QUOTES = {  # binding -> exact text in edition v0 (markdown emphasis and line breaks removed before matching)
    "q_toothless": "Anthropic's charter is legally real and legally toothless.",
    "q_365b": "§365(b) gives directors no duty to any person on account of a public-benefit interest",
}


def git(*a: str) -> str:
    return subprocess.run(["git", *a], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout


def b3(p: Path) -> str:
    return blake3.blake3(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def label(t: str) -> str:
    return LABELS.get(t, t + " *")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- preconditions
def preflight(cb: dict, inputs: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    errs = []
    r = subprocess.run(["uv", "run", "--quiet", str(DAG_TOOL), "status"], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        errs.append("dag.py status is not all ok:\n" + "\n".join(l for l in r.stdout.splitlines() if not l.startswith("ok")))
    for p in inputs:
        if not git("ls-files", "--", p).strip():
            errs.append(f"input not committed: {p}")
    dirty = git("status", "--porcelain", "--", *inputs).strip()
    if dirty:
        errs.append("inputs modified since the last commit:\n" + dirty)
    return errs


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- bindings + charts
def flags_sql(scores: Path, h: str) -> str:
    return (f"SELECT d.window_id FROM '{scores / 'deberta.parquet'}' d JOIN '{scores / 'modernbert.parquet'}' m "
            f"USING (window_id, hypothesis_id) WHERE d.hypothesis_id = '{h}' AND d.p_entail >= .5 AND m.p_entail >= .5")


def earnings(cb: dict, b: dict) -> tuple[list[tuple], list[tuple]]:
    con = duckdb.connect()
    scores = ROOT / cb["ec_scores"]
    as_of = str(con.execute(f"SELECT max(report_date) FROM read_csv('{EC / 'calls.tsv'}')").fetchone()[0])
    types = [r["id"] for r in csv.DictReader((ROOT / cb["file"]).open(), delimiter="\t") if r["group"] == "risk_type"]
    con.execute(f"""CREATE TABLE calls AS SELECT symbol, fiscal_year, fiscal_quarter, report_date
        FROM read_csv('{EC / "calls.tsv"}')
        WHERE (duplicate_of IS NULL OR duplicate_of = '') AND n_paragraphs > 2 AND report_date <= DATE '{as_of}'""")
    con.execute(f"""CREATE TABLE w AS SELECT window_id, symbol, fiscal_year, fiscal_quarter, report_date::DATE AS report_date,
            regexp_matches(text, '{RISK_WORD}') AS lex,
            window_id IN ({flags_sql(scores, 'ai_risk')}) AS ai_risk
        FROM '{EC / "ai-windows.parquet"}'""")
    con.execute("""CREATE TABLE cw AS SELECT c.*, bool_or(w.lex) AS lex, bool_or(w.ai_risk) AS nli
        FROM calls c LEFT JOIN w USING (symbol, fiscal_year, fiscal_quarter) GROUP BY ALL""")
    series = con.execute(f"""SELECT year(report_date) AS year, count(*) AS calls,
            round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE lex) / count(*), 2), round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE nli) / count(*), 2)
        FROM cw WHERE year(report_date) >= {FIRST_YEAR} GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1""").fetchall()
    since = f"DATE '{as_of}' - INTERVAL 1 YEAR"
    con.execute(f"CREATE TABLE ttm AS SELECT * FROM w WHERE report_date > {since} AND report_date <= DATE '{as_of}' AND ai_risk")
    ranking = []
    for t in types:
        firms = con.execute(f"SELECT count(DISTINCT symbol) FROM ttm WHERE window_id IN ({flags_sql(scores, t)})").fetchone()[0]
        ranking.append((t, label(t), firms))
    ranking.sort(key=lambda r: (-r[2], r[0]))
    b.update(as_of=as_of, ec_year_last=str(series[-1][0]), ec_pct_witness_last=f"{series[-1][3]:.1f}",
             ec_pre2023_max=f"{max(r[3] for r in series if r[0] < 2023):.1f}",
             ec_ttm_risk_firms=str(con.execute("SELECT count(DISTINCT symbol) FROM ttm").fetchone()[0]),
             ec_top3=", ".join(f"{r[1].rstrip(' *')} ({r[2]})" for r in ranking[:3]))
    return series, ranking


def plot_earnings(series, ranking, b: dict, codebook: str) -> None:
    matplotlib, plt = deck_charts.setup()
    S = deck_charts
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4.2), facecolor=S.SURFACE)
    S.style(ax)
    years = [r[0] for r in series]
    for col, color, name in ((2, S.S1, 'Mentions "risk" next to AI (no model)'), (3, S.S2, f"Both models: AI framed as a risk ({codebook})")):
        ys = [float(r[col]) for r in series]
        ax.plot(years, ys, color=color, lw=2, marker="o", ms=4.5, mec=S.SURFACE, mew=1.5, label=name)
        ax.annotate(f"{ys[-1]:.1f}%", (years[-1], ys[-1]), xytext=(8, 0), textcoords="offset points",
                    va="center", color=S.INK, fontsize=10, fontweight="bold")
    ax.set_xticks(years, [str(y) if y != years[-1] else f"{y}\n(to {b['as_of'][5:]})" for y in years], fontsize=9)
    ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(matplotlib.ticker.FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"{v:.0f}%"))
    ax.set_ylim(0, None)
    ax.set_title("Share of S&P 500 earnings calls where AI is discussed as a risk", loc="left",
                 color=S.INK, fontsize=12, fontweight="bold", pad=22)
    ax.text(0, 1.02, "Calls per calendar year; denominator is every unique, non-stub S&P 500 call in the corpus",
            transform=ax.transAxes, color=S.INK2, fontsize=9)
    ax.legend(loc="upper left", frameon=False, fontsize=9, labelcolor=S.INK)
    fig.text(0.01, 0.01, f"Source: defeatbeta/yahoo-finance-data transcripts (ODC-BY). Model line: risk codebook {codebook}, "
             "witness proposal, not hand-verified.", color=S.INK2, fontsize=7.5)
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.03, 1, 1))

def table(path: str) -> list[dict]:
    with (ROOT / path).open() as f:
        return list(csv.DictReader((l for l in f if not l.startswith("#")), delimiter="\t"))


def other_bindings(cb: dict, b: dict) -> None:
    qi = {r["intent"]: r for r in table(FIXED["question_intents"])}
    b.update(q_revenue_pct=f"{float(qi['q_revenue']['pct_of_ai_questions']):.1f}",
             q_controls_pct=f"{float(qi['q_controls']['pct_of_ai_questions']):.1f}")
    ds = {r["risk_type"]: r for r in table(cb["dialogue"])}
    b.update(ds_exec_safety=f"{float(ds['safety_ethics']['executives_pct']):.0f}",
             ds_hn_safety=f"{float(ds['safety_ethics']['hn_anthropic_pct']):.0f}",
             ds_wp_safety=f"{float(ds['safety_ethics']['wikipedia_pct']):.0f}",
             ds_sec_cyber=f"{float(ds['cyber']['hn_security_pct']):.0f}")
    cve = table(FIXED["cve_monthly_ai"])
    b.update(cve_claude_total=f"{sum(int(r['n_credit_claude']) for r in cve):,}",
             cve_ai_total=f"{sum(int(r['n_ai_credited']) for r in cve):,}",
             cve_first=cve[0]["month"], cve_last=cve[-1]["month"])


def quotes(b: dict) -> list[str]:
    text = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", git("show", f"{PAPER_V0}:{PAPER}").replace("**", "").replace("*", ""))
    errs = []
    for k, q in QUOTES.items():
        if q not in text:
            errs.append(f"quote {k} not found in {PAPER}@{PAPER_V0}: {q}")
        b[k] = q
    return errs


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- render
CAPTION_OK = re.compile(r"\{\{\w+\}\}|v0\.\d+(-draft)?|S&P 500|12 months|33,000\+|≥ 0\.5|edition v0")


def render(b: dict) -> tuple[str, list[str]]:
    tpl = TEMPLATE.read_text()
    errs = []
    for i, line in enumerate(tpl.splitlines(), 1):
        if 'class="src"' in line and re.search(r"\d", CAPTION_OK.sub("", line)):
            errs.append(f"deck.template.md:{i}: unbound number in caption")
    missing = sorted(set(re.findall(r"\{\{(\w+)\}\}", tpl)) - set(b))
    errs += [f"unresolved binding {{{{{m}}}}}" for m in missing]
    return re.sub(r"\{\{(\w+)\}\}", lambda m: b.get(m.group(1), m.group(0)), tpl), errs


def build(codebook: str) -> tuple[dict[str, bytes], list[str]]:
    cb = CODEBOOKS[codebook]
    inputs = [cb["file"], cb["ec_scores"], cb["dialogue"], *FIXED.values(), "corpus/earnings-calls/calls.tsv",
              "corpus/earnings-calls/ai-windows.parquet", "deck/deck.template.md", "scripts/build_edition.py",
              "scripts/deck_charts.py", "dag.lock.tsv"]
    errs = preflight(cb, inputs)
    if errs:
        return {}, errs
    head = git("rev-parse", "HEAD").strip()
    b = {"codebook": codebook, "codebook_status": cb["status"], "source_commit": head[:12], "paper_v0": PAPER_V0,
         "generated_notice": f"<!-- GENERATED by scripts/build_edition.py --codebook {codebook} from {head}. "
                             "Edit deck/deck.template.md, not this file. -->"}
    errs += quotes(b)
    OUT_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    series, ranking = earnings(cb, b)
    plot_earnings(series, ranking, b, codebook)
    deck_charts.OUT = OUT_DIR
    deck_charts.cve(*deck_charts.setup())
    other_bindings(cb, b)
    md, rerrs = render(b)
    errs += rerrs
    outs = {"DECK.md": md.encode()}
    for n in ("ai-risk-by-year.svg", "risk-ranking-ttm.svg", "cve-ai-credit.svg"):
        outs[f"deck/{n}"] = (OUT_DIR / n).read_bytes()
    stamp = {
        "edition_of": head,
        "codebook": {"risk": codebook, "risk_file": cb["file"], "risk_blake3": b3(ROOT / cb["file"]),
                     "question_intents": "corpus/earnings-calls/codebook-questions-v0.1.tsv"},
        "rule": "positive = DeBERTa and ModernBERT both >= 0.5",
        "dag_lock_blake3": b3(ROOT / "dag.lock.tsv"),
        "paper_v0": f"{PAPER}@{PAPER_V0}",
        "tools": {"python": "duckdb==2.0.0 matplotlib==3.10.7 blake3==1.0.11",
                  "render": "npx @marp-team/marp-cli@4.1.2 DECK.md --pptx --allow-local-files"},
        "bindings": {k: v for k, v in sorted(b.items()) if k != "generated_notice"},
        "inputs": {p: b3(ROOT / p) for p in sorted(inputs) if (ROOT / p).is_file()},
        "outputs": {k: blake3.blake3(v).hexdigest() for k, v in sorted(outs.items())},
        "references": {p: b3(ROOT / p) for p in (FIXED["question_chart"], FIXED["dialogue_chart"])},
    }
    outs["deck/STAMP.json"] = (json.dumps(stamp, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n").encode()
    return outs, errs


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--codebook", required=True, choices=sorted(CODEBOOKS))
    ap.add_argument("--check", action="store_true", help="rebuild and compare; write nothing that differs")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    before = {p: (ROOT / p).read_bytes() for p in ("DECK.md", "deck/ai-risk-by-year.svg", "deck/risk-ranking-ttm.svg",
                                                   "deck/cve-ai-credit.svg", "deck/STAMP.json") if (ROOT / p).exists()}
    outs, errs = build(a.codebook)
    if errs:
        for p, v in before.items():   # leave the tree as it was
            (ROOT / p).write_bytes(v)
        print("build failed:\n  " + "\n  ".join(errs), file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    if a.check:
        diff = [p for p, v in outs.items() if before.get(p) != v]
        for p, v in before.items():
            (ROOT / p).write_bytes(v)
        print("edition is current" if not diff else "edition would change: " + ", ".join(diff))
        return 1 if diff else 0
    for p, v in outs.items():
        (ROOT / p).write_bytes(v)
    print(f"built edition of {outs and json.loads(outs['deck/STAMP.json'])['edition_of'][:12]} "
          f"with risk codebook {a.codebook}. Review `git diff`, then commit.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
