Intent (Sloane, 2026-11-04): articles are built from Descartes output, modularly. Nothing an article states about its own verification is written by hand, and a statement whose evidence is invalidated fixes or flags itself.

First article: anthropic-pbc `docs/anthropic-contrapunctus.md` (claims `claims/anthropic-contrapunctus.tsv`, sources `sources/MANIFEST.tsv`).

## 1. One authority for source text
Descartes ingests an article's pinned sources (its MANIFEST) and claims, runs the recorded recipes and owns the derived text. The article repository holds the paper, the claims and the manifest, and runs no recipe itself. Today anthropic-pbc runs pdftotext and html-to-text locally and records the result with `descartes derive`: two places produce text. Needs the paper-registry adapter (descartes docs/public-mirror/integration-status.md).

## 2. Generated status, never hand counts
The article's "Verification status" (claims ok / failing, per cause, per claim) is emitted by Descartes as data and included in the article at build time. Found stale: §5.3 still says "51 of 60" while the check reports 72 ok / 22 failing.

## 3. Invalidation propagates
Every article statement that rests on evidence is a claim with `rests_on`, including composite and negative statements. When a leaf fails, or a pinned source contradicts it, every statement resting on it fails and the article marks it at build time, without hand edits. Case: the paper said three times that the S-1 is silent on the four-model unauthorized-access incident; the S-1 risk factors disclose it. A negative claim ("source A does not mention X") needs a checkable form, e.g. a recorded search over the derived text, which fails when a match appears. Design open.

## 4. PDF whitespace in the recipe
README §8: whitespace conversion is part of the recorded derivation, never the checker. The PDF recipe keeps printed line breaks (and the RSP's U+200B at line edges), so 18 faithful quotations fail (Constitution 11, Report 6, RSP 1). First test case for 1–3.

## 5. Rendered pages
Pages with external stylesheets are refused by html-to-text static-v1: trail #25. Blocks the Public Benefit Fund announcement, DGCL, two SEC pages, and two Anthropic pages (Q048, Q084).

content.text:
I fixed all three errors in the paper and opened Entire trail #26 for the coordination between Descartes and articles.

**The fixes (commit `0655261`):**
- **S-1 contradiction.** §6.3.1, Appendix A and GOV-10 no longer call the S-1 silent. §6.3.1 now quotes the S-1's risk factor: "Four of our models gained unauthorized access to real third-party systems". That is new claim Q094, and it occurs exactly once in the S-1.
- **Wrong source in §7.1.** "Pacing the frontier" is now attributed to the S-1, with its own scope: industry-wide standards, and in its words the call "does not describe our own model development".
- **Stale counts.** I took the hand-written "51 of 60" out of §5.3. The section now points to the unedited check record, which the build will replace with Descartes's own output. Figure 1 is withdrawn for the same reason: its counts were typed into `figures/build.py`.
- **Check result:** 73 claims pass and 22 fail, the same 22 as before. Q094 passes.

**Trail #26 covers what you described:**
1. **One authority for source text.** Descartes ingests an article's pinned sources and claims and owns the derived text. The article repo runs no recipes itself.
2. **Generated status.** Counts, per-claim states and charts of them come from Descartes output at build time.
3. **Invalidation propagates.** Every statement that rests on evidence becomes a claim, so when its evidence fails or a source contradicts it, the statement fails and the paper marks it automatically. Statements that a source says nothing about something (like "the S-1 is silent") need a checkable form, such as a recorded search of the source text that fails when a match appears. That design is open in the trail.
4. **Line breaks from PDFs are handled in the recipe**, with the 18 failing quotes as the first test.
5. **Rendered web pages**, linked to trail #25.

The S-1 error didn't fix itself because "the S-1 is silent" was never a claim, only prose, so nothing could invalidate it. Item 3 is for that case.

The other three charts in the gallery (figs 2–4) also take their numbers typed into `figures/build.py`, not generated from the claims. They will go stale the same way, and they belong under item 2. Pulling them now is your call.
Well, also, the intro to the S1 and the S1, I believe, are still the same filing But it is important to be very, very, very, very precise about where we find shit

**Short IDs: yes for sources, no for the paper.** And the IDs should be computed from the text, not assigned.

- **In pinned sources, yes.** Descartes would split each source's text into blocks and give each block a short ID, such as 5 characters of its BLAKE3 hash. A quote then cites `s1a1 · p.49 · k7f3q`: readable and quotable, and anyone can recompute it from the pinned bytes. It also solves the repeated passages: the ID picks the occurrence, so Q010's seven appearances become seven distinct, citable locations without lengthening any quote. Pinned bytes never change, so the IDs never drift.
- **Computed, not assigned.** An assigned ID needs a registry that someone maintains, which is the hand-written-counts problem again. A hash-derived ID needs no registry, and Descartes already checks it is unique within the document. Five base-32 characters give about 33 million values, so a clash within one filing is unlikely, and if one happens the check fails loudly.
- **In the paper, no.** The paper changes every day, so IDs computed from its text would change on every edit. It already has stable IDs, the claim labels (Q094 and so on), and the build can print them as markers beside each quotation. The trail runs from paper marker to claim row to source block to bytes.

Intent (Sloane, 2026-11-04): monitoring around Descartes for efficiency.

## Direction: a periodic full-corpus run
"We want to be able to run Descartes over our entire corpus every once in a while. So the direction for optimization is that." (Sloane, 2026-11-04.) Optimize for the full sweep, not for one paper.

Scale today, anthropic-pbc alone: about 11 GB of pinned bulk (`.hncorpus` 5.4 GB, `.eccorpus` 2.8 GB, `.rfcorpus` 1.5 GB, `.cvecorpus` 1.3 GB, the others ~30 MB) plus 38 MB committed under `corpus/`; the paper's sources are ~20 MB. A full run is roughly 500× the paper check. The Praxis lake adds more.

What that implies:
- **Measure throughput:** bytes per second and claims per second, per step, so a full run's cost is predictable before it starts. The time budget for a full run is Sloane's to set.
- **One pass per artifact:** check every quote against an artifact in a single scan, not one scan per quote.
- **Offsets before search:** corpus rows already carry character offsets and BLAKE3; verifying a recorded slice costs the slice, not the artifact.
- **Bounded memory:** stream artifacts; parallelize across them.
- **Skip by content:** an incremental run skips any (artifact digest, claim digest, binary digest) already verified. The periodic full run re-does everything and must reach the same root; that agreement is the check on the incremental path.

**What that means for the design:**
- **Throughput comes first:** measure bytes per second and claims per second at each step, so the cost of a full run is known before it starts. How long a full run is allowed to take is your call; the trail leaves that open.
- **One pass per source:** check all the quotes in a source in a single read, not one read per quote. That fivefold gap between wall time and CPU time may be exactly this.
- **Offsets before search:** corpus rows already record character offsets and a BLAKE3 hash, so checking one costs the length of the quote, not the length of the source.
- **Skip what hasn't changed:** an incremental run skips any source, claim and Descartes build it has already verified together. The periodic full run redoes everything and must reach the same root hash, which is how we know the shortcut is honest.
- **Bounded memory and no second copy:** stream sources and spread them across cores. Copying 11 GB into the Descartes store would double disk use, so the store should reuse the pinned bytes already on disk where its integrity rules allow.

The short source IDs from before fit this too. Hashing each block once per source gives cheap, stable locations across the whole corpus.

Correctness is always going to come first. Right? Like, we don't want to let privilege one thing over whatever, but we want to make sure that we're running this as well as efficiently as we can, that the outputs are good, and that's creating reliable output because a lot of stuff rests on it. # Circles of assumption

A derivation such as PDF → text is never simply "faithful" or "unfaithful".
Each part of the content gets a colour: the highest circle at which that part
is verified, together with the measured gap.

| Circle | What is assumed or checked | Instrument |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | The source bytes, identified by digest. This is the only thing assumed. | none |
| 1 | Conservation laws measured with one instrument: every word kept, every inked pixel accounted for | poppler (`pdftotext -bbox`, `pdftoppm`) |
| 2 | The same measurement confirmed by an independent instrument | tesseract OCR of the raster, which never sees poppler's text layer |
| 3 | An untrusted proposal (LLM) that passes circles 1–2 | an LLM witness, checked by `descartes` |
| 4 | Human discernment: what no mechanical check can settle | a person |

Rasters, text layers and OCR output are not ground truth. They are
derivations from circle 0, re-run on every check and kept only as digests in
`artifacts/fidelity/<name>.instruments.tsv`. If a re-run gives a different
digest, the instruments are not reproducible and the check fails. Because
everything can be regenerated from the source, only the source is assumed.

## First measurement: the Gemini transcript (2026-11-02)

`sh stage1/fidelity.sh` produced
`artifacts/fidelity/Secure-Alternatives-to-Iroh-P2P.tsv`:

| Component | Circle | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| source bytes | 0 | reproducible from the digest |
| text (words) | 1 | 10,898 / 10,910 (99.89%) of text-layer words are present in `pdftotext` output |
| text (words) | 2 | 10,619 / 10,910 (97.33%) confirmed by OCR at the same position |
| text position | 0 | not captured: the plain-text derivation has no coordinates |
| non-text ink | 0 | 2.41% of inked pixels lie outside every word box, in 17 regions: table grids and section rules |
| tables | 0 | not captured: row/column pairings are unverified |
| reading order | 4 | open |

The largest unaccounted region on page 3 (42.5,143 → 570,307.5 pt) is
exactly the "Comparison Across Your Requirements" table grid. The ink check
found the table without being told to look for one. Any claim that depends
on which cell sits in which row therefore rests on circle 0 until a table
proposal passes a geometric check.

The 2.67% of words OCR does not confirm are mostly code (monospace
punctuation, `::`, `->`) and the box-drawing characters in diagrams. These
are differences between instruments, and they stay visible in the per-page
rows rather than being averaged away.

## Parameters (recorded in every report)

| Parameter | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Scale | 2 px/pt (144 dpi) | Enough resolution for OCR. Coordinates are exact multiples of points. |
| Ink threshold | < 250 of 255 | Chrome draws table rules in light grey. A mid-grey threshold (128) missed every one of them, which the first run showed: 0 regions. |
| Mask margin | 1 pt | Glyph ink extends slightly past the font's box. |
| Minimum region | 40 px | Anti-aliasing specks are counted in the totals but not listed as regions. |

These are assumptions too, so they are printed at the top of every report.

## Next, in order

1. **Table proposals (circle 3).** An LLM proposes cells as page + box +

   explains. A table that passes moves its pairings from circle 0 to circle 3.
2. **Name the lost words.** Report the 12 words the plain-text derivation
   dropped.
3. **Second text-layer instrument.** A content-stream reader, so circle 2
   for text does not rest on OCR alone.

That draft and this design share the structure. They differ in these places:

- It puts the 300 dpi raster in circle 0. A raster is the output of a

# Shared producer contract

Praxis owns the common emission and semantic-lake contracts for participating producers. Producer repositories retain their methods, source acquisition, authorship and independent version history. The [root README](../README.md) governs Praxis; each producer's README governs its own module. This is a shared behavior contract, not a second cross-repository roadmap.

## Before adding or changing an emitter

Reusable slide metadata is aggregated by the [central slide catalog](../catalog/SLIDES.md).
Keep one plain source manifest per library and treat old component bindings as
legacy provenance. The aggregate/native catalog must not acquire React or another
framework dependency merely to browse or combine records. Unconverted visual
layouts remain explicitly unconverted.

1. Use the [design primitive](../design/README.md) and [composable presentation contract](../design/research-presentation.md). The [research template](../design/research-template.md) is one starting composition. Keep relevant facts, claims, sources, version and limitations linked from the opening.
2. Reuse the [offline renderer](../render/README.md) and [composable HTML parts](../design/components.py) for new pages, line/bar figures, relationship views and audience-selected HTML/JSON-LD/N-Triples exports. Use the [central report writer](../report_writer/README.md) for the PDF/report path where appropriate. Add a thin producer adapter for a missing input shape; do not fork the styles or create a competing website generator.
3. Emit from pinned producer data and methods. Keep dataset, metric, unit, original locators, missingness, source version and transformation identity. One selected record set must drive the human-facing output and linked data. Do not harmonize conflicting judgments or merge authorization because byte hashes match.
4. Preserve authorship. An independently authored working paper does not become an Ethical Capital opinion because the firm hosts or aggregates it. Official firm treatment requires an explicit version and release authority; a rendering task alone is not that authority.
5. Keep export audience, publication identity, source checks, signature results and review separate. Public output must be an explicitly eligible dependency closure. Private material must never be present in hidden HTML, client bundles, source downloads, structured data or indexes of a public export.

Existing sealed publications and producer-specific emitters are not automatically migrated by a documentation pointer. Preserve their bytes, pins and signing protocols. When changing an actual emitter, prove its adapter and regenerate/check the affected output through the producer's normal revision process. The current website is not rebuilt merely by adopting this contract.

## Data belongs to one governed semantic lake

Before adding implementation code, ask whether the behavior is needed and whether
an existing component already provides it. Prefer a maintained dependency with a
small adapter over a new parser, cryptographic primitive or storage engine. Compare
total maintenance, transitive dependencies, resource use, licensing and failure
behavior; fewer lines of our code alone is not sufficient. Pin the selected tool and
test its input/output boundary. For PDF intake, inspect the existing extraction and
rendering paths before proposing another PDF parser. Record an actual missing
capability before writing custom code.

Software and capability records should join the governed catalog by stable identity,
version, owner, supported inputs/outputs, rights and reuse evidence. They point to
the authoritative repository/package; lake participation does not move source code
or deployment secrets into a data table. The referenced software repository remains
to be identified. DuckLake is a storage/query component behind this contract, not a
replacement for authorization or a reason to duplicate the software registry.

The [semantic-lake contract](semantic-lake.md) and [catalog contract](../catalog/README.md) are canonical. Praxis manages catalog identity, shared metadata and custody/placement requirements. Bulk source and derived datasets, source snapshots, claim/source records and research-question datasets participate in that one governed lake under their real owner, audience and rights scope.

Local files, caches, SQLite/vector indexes and per-repository directories can be staging, retained source pins or rebuildable projections. They must not quietly become a second authoritative private research system. A manifest saying a location exists is not evidence that bytes were stored there.

Before calling a transfer complete, obtain an actual placement/write receipt with:

- owner and audience/rights scope, dataset and immutable artifact identity;
- actual backend, bucket/container and object key or equivalent location;
- content digest, byte count and backend version where available;
- successful write plus digest/readback evidence;
- authorized reader/writer identity and allowed/denied-access evidence for private scope;
- catalog selection tied to that exact completed receipt, with retries and partial writes accounted for.

Do not guess a bucket/key from a dataset name, use a shared reference bucket as a private fallback, or promote a cached source into lake custody by renaming it. A public source can lead to private analysis. Equal bytes can have different custody and rights records. Keep source attribution and restrictions attached through derivation, search, export and delivery.

**Current boundary:** Praxis has a working local metadata catalog and offline renderer. A general lake object/manifest service, tenant authorization, transfer/recovery receipts and their runtime acceptance are not established by these tools. Existing backends must be verified for the particular dataset and scope before use. Until that succeeds, retain the current authorized bytes and pin their location as staging; report the missing placement/receipt rather than moving or publishing them. Adoption does not authorize a data migration, new bucket, credential grant or public upload.

## What producers and agents should do proactively

When work adds a dataset, emitter or off-machine copy, check this contract. Reuse central generation rather than starting another theme or generator. Register the producer's pinned metadata with the catalog; distinguish registration from storage, review and publication. Ask the coordinating owner to resolve a missing lake placement, access boundary or receipt, and preserve the existing source until resolved. Do not silently invent a private store or mark the task complete from a tool-success label.

Use the existing cross-repository coordination pointer for shared sequencing. Public producers need only the public Praxis contracts to build; do not copy private coordination plans, access details or research payloads into public repositories. No dependency on a private Dark checkout is introduced into public compilation.

- **Tests first.** I wrote four tests before the rule existed. The two that need the rule failed, and the two that check it doesn't over-reach passed. Then I added the rule to Descartes's claims check.

#!/bin/sh
# article.sh ARTICLE_ROOT CLAIMS_FILE... : verify an article repository's inputs,
# then check its claims, with the same rules the loop applies to this repository.
#
#   1. sources/MANIFEST.tsv (id role fetched url path bytes blake3): every row's
#      file exists under sources/ with that size and BLAKE3, and every file in
#      sources/ (except the manifest) has a row.
#   2. derived/recipes.tsv (output input tool args): only the loop's tools, each
#      with its one argument shape; inputs are manifest sources; each recipe is
#      re-run and must reproduce its output byte for byte; every derived/*.txt
#      has a recipe.
#   3. descartes check on each claims file.
#
# Every problem is reported, not just the first; the exit status is 1 if any
# step failed. No clock or host enters the report. Unlike the loop, this runs
# no sandbox, and says so. The binary is $DESCARTES or ./descartes beside this
# repository's build; tools/html_to_text.py is this repository's recipe.
set -u
[ $# -ge 2 ] || { echo "usage: article.sh ARTICLE_ROOT CLAIMS_FILE..." >&2; exit 64; }
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
ROOT=$1; shift
BIN=${DESCARTES:-}
[ -n "$BIN" ] && [ -x "$BIN" ] || { echo "article: set DESCARTES to a descartes binary" >&2; exit 64; }
HTML="$HERE/tools/html_to_text.py"
tab=$(printf '\t')
bad=0
TMP=$(mktemp -d) || exit 70
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT INT TERM
note() { printf '%s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf 'FAIL\t%s\n' "$*"; bad=1; }
sha256_of() {
  if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum < "$1" | awk '{print $1}'
  else shasum -a 256 < "$1" | awk '{print $1}'; fi
}
safe_rel() { case "$1" in ''|/*|-*|../*|*/../*|*/..|*/./*|./*) return 1 ;; esac; return 0; }

[ -f "$M" ] || { fail "$M missing"; exit 1; }
: > "$TMP/listed"
rows=0
while IFS="$tab" read -r id role fetched url path bytes b3 rest || [ -n "${id:-}" ]; do

  rows=$((rows + 1))
  [ -z "${rest:-}" ] || fail "$M: $id: more than 7 columns"
  safe_rel "$path" || { fail "$M: $id: path must be relative and plain: $path"; continue; }
  f="sources/$path"
  printf '%s\n' "$f" >> "$TMP/listed"
  if [ ! -f "$f" ] || [ -L "$f" ]; then fail "$M: $id: $f missing or not a regular file"; continue; fi
  got_bytes=$(wc -c < "$f" | tr -d ' ')
  [ "$got_bytes" = "$bytes" ] || fail "$M: $id: $f has $got_bytes bytes, manifest says $bytes"
  got_b3=$("$BIN" hash "$f" | cut -f2)
  [ "$got_b3" = "$b3" ] || fail "$M: $id: $f BLAKE3 $got_b3, manifest says $b3"
done < "$M"
note "article: manifest  $rows rows"
find sources -type f ! -name MANIFEST.tsv | LC_ALL=C sort > "$TMP/present"
LC_ALL=C sort -u "$TMP/listed" > "$TMP/listed.sorted"
comm -23 "$TMP/present" "$TMP/listed.sorted" | while read -r f; do printf 'FAIL\t%s is not in %s\n' "$f" "$M"; done > "$TMP/unlisted"
[ -s "$TMP/unlisted" ] && { cat "$TMP/unlisted"; bad=1; }

# --- 2. recipes ------------------------------------------------------------
R=derived/recipes.tsv
: > "$TMP/recipied"
if [ -f "$R" ]; then

    case "$output" in ''|'#'*) continue ;; esac

    case "$output" in derived/*) ;; *) fail "$R: $output: output must be under derived/"; continue ;; esac
    rm -f "$TMP/out"
    case "$tool" in
      pdftotext)

        version=$(pdftotext -v 2>&1 | sed -n '1p')

        version="$(/usr/bin/python3 -I -B "$HTML" --version); $(/usr/bin/python3 -I -B --version 2>&1); script-sha256:$(sha256_of "$HTML")"

        ;;
    esac
    if [ ! -f "$output" ]; then fail "$R: $output: missing (run the recipe)"; continue; fi
    cmp -s "$TMP/out" "$output" || { fail "$R: $output: not reproducible from $input with $version"; continue; }
    note "ok	re-derived $output from $input with $version: byte-identical"
  done < "$R"
fi
if [ -d derived ]; then
  find derived -type f -name '*.txt' | LC_ALL=C sort > "$TMP/dtxt"
  LC_ALL=C sort -u "$TMP/recipied" > "$TMP/recipied.sorted"
  comm -23 "$TMP/dtxt" "$TMP/recipied.sorted" | while read -r f; do printf 'FAIL\t%s has no recipe in %s\n' "$f" "$R"; done > "$TMP/norecipe"
  [ -s "$TMP/norecipe" ] && { cat "$TMP/norecipe"; bad=1; }
fi

# --- 3. claims -------------------------------------------------------------
for c in "$@"; do
  "$BIN" check "$c" > "$TMP/check" 2>&1

  grep -v '^ok' "$TMP/check"
  [ $status -eq 0 ] || bad=1
done

exit $bad

# Negative suite for stage1/article.sh: a clean article passes, and each kind
# of tampering is refused with its own message. Usage: DESCARTES=bin test-article.sh
set -u
ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd -P)
: "${DESCARTES:?set DESCARTES to a descartes binary}"
TMP=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/descartes-article-test.XXXXXX") || exit 70
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT HUP INT TERM
tab=$(printf '\t')
failures=0

# A minimal article: one HTML source, its recipe, one claim.
fixture() {
  rm -rf "$TMP/a"; mkdir -p "$TMP/a/sources" "$TMP/a/derived" "$TMP/a/claims"
  cp "$ROOT/tests/html/static.html" "$TMP/a/sources/page.html"
  b=$(wc -c < "$TMP/a/sources/page.html" | tr -d ' ')
  h=$("$DESCARTES" hash "$TMP/a/sources/page.html" | cut -f2)
  printf 'id\trole\tfetched\turl\tpath\tbytes\tblake3\npage\tcase\t2026-11-04\thttps://example.org/page\tpage.html\t%s\t%s\n' "$b" "$h" > "$TMP/a/sources/MANIFEST.tsv"
  printf 'derived/page.txt\tsources/page.html\thtml-to-text\tstatic-v1\n' > "$TMP/a/derived/recipes.tsv"
  cp "$ROOT/tests/html/static.txt" "$TMP/a/derived/page.txt"
  printf 'C1\t-\tllm:test prompt=unrecorded\tthe page says capital is substantial\tderived/page.txt\tsubstantial and increasing capital\n' > "$TMP/a/claims/c.tsv"
}
run() { DESCARTES="$DESCARTES" sh "$ROOT/stage1/article.sh" "$TMP/a" claims/c.tsv > "$TMP/out" 2>&1; }
expect_pass() {
  if run; then echo "ok    $1"; else echo "FAIL  $1: clean article refused"; cat "$TMP/out"; failures=$((failures + 1)); fi
}
expect_fail() { # name, message the report must contain
  if run; then echo "FAIL  $1: accepted"; failures=$((failures + 1))
  elif grep -qF -e "$2" "$TMP/out"; then echo "ok    $1"
  else echo "FAIL  $1: refused without '$2'"; cat "$TMP/out"; failures=$((failures + 1)); fi

# Evidence is a recipe output, never a raw source: raw HTML keeps comments,
# scripts and markup in which a quote can match unseen. A prompt digest names
# a file committed at HEAD under prompts/, not whatever is on disk.
LC_ALL=C sort -u "$TMP/recipied" > "$TMP/recipied.sorted"
: > "$TMP/digests"
for c in "$@"; do
  [ -f "$c" ] || { fail "$c: claims file missing"; continue; }
  awk -F'\t' 'NF >= 6 && $0 !~ /^#/ { print FNR "\t" $5 }' "$c" | while IFS="$tab" read -r n p; do
    [ "$p" = "-" ] && continue
    grep -qxF -e "$p" "$TMP/recipied.sorted" || printf 'FAIL\t%s:%s: evidence %s is not a recipe output in %s\n' "$c" "$n" "$p" "$R"
  done > "$TMP/cite"
  [ -s "$TMP/cite" ] && { cat "$TMP/cite"; bad=1; }
  awk -F'\t' 'NF >= 6 && $0 !~ /^#/ { print $3 }' "$c" | tr ' ' '\n' | sed -n 's/^prompt=sha256:\([0-9a-f]\{64\}\)$/\1/p' >> "$TMP/digests"
done
if [ -s "$TMP/digests" ]; then
  if git rev-parse --verify -q HEAD > /dev/null 2>&1; then
    git ls-tree -r --name-only HEAD -- prompts/ | while read -r f; do
      git show "HEAD:$f" | { if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum; else shasum -a 256; fi; } | awk '{print $1}'
    done | LC_ALL=C sort -u > "$TMP/committed"
    LC_ALL=C sort -u "$TMP/digests" | comm -23 - "$TMP/committed" | while read -r d; do
      printf 'FAIL\tprompt=sha256:%s: no prompt file with this digest is committed at HEAD under prompts/\n' "$d"
    done > "$TMP/untracked"
    [ -s "$TMP/untracked" ] && { cat "$TMP/untracked"; bad=1; }
    note "article: prompts  $(LC_ALL=C sort -u "$TMP/digests" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') digests named, checked against HEAD $(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"
  else
    fail "claims name prompt digests, but $ROOT is not a git repository with a HEAD, so committed prompts cannot be checked"

# Adversarial audit of the verification chain, 2026-11-04

Question (Sloane: "really lock this down"): how can a wrong or unverifiable
record pass the checks on this paper without any check failing? An LLM agent
audited the chain read-only and reproduced its cases on scratch copies. Each
finding is listed with what was done. Fixes are on the Descartes branch
`witness-prompt-digest` (commits 1a44f60, 8ef1b42, d828de8, e7b3cb6), **not
merged**: see "Decisions open".

State when audited: all 15 sources matched their BLAKE3 in
`sources/MANIFEST.tsv`, and all 7 `derived/*.txt` rebuilt byte-identical from
their recipes. Nothing had drifted; the gaps were that nothing would catch it.

| # | Finding (reproduced unless marked) | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | No gate runs `descartes check`: the hooks and CI run only `scripts/seal.py check`, so "passed" means an `ok` line read from a doc, not an exit code. | **Open.** The hook and workflow files belong to another session's uncommitted work. |
| 2 | The check trusts whatever bytes are on disk: an edited `derived/*.txt` or raw source passed; `descartes derive` records without running the tool; three rows quote raw HTML. | **Closed for articles** by `stage1/article.sh`: manifest bytes and BLAKE3, recipes replayed byte for byte, every derived file has a recipe, evidence must be a recipe output. Binding this inside `descartes check` itself is Entire trail #26. |
| 3 | A quote can pass without saying what the source says: no word boundary, no length floor, spans across headings and page numbers; a match inside an HTML comment passed. Live case Q022b dropped "necessarily". | **Partly closed.** Quotes match whole words only (d828de8). Q022b requoted (ceb603f). Raw HTML refused as evidence. **Open:** a minimum quote length, refusing spans across paragraph breaks, and storing context with the evidence. |
| 4 | The witness rule was easy to get past: `LLM:`, a leading space, `llm-x`, a second `prompt=`, and any file on disk under `prompts/`. | **Closed.** Witness kinds are a closed set (`human`, `llm`, `org`, `doi`, `arxiv`); exactly one `prompt=`; the digest must name a file committed at HEAD. **Open:** tying each row to the step that produced it. |
| 5 | Nothing checks the review or steps files: 24 claim labels have no review row and 20 review labels have no claim (split and renamed labels); review `context` is not verbatim in most rows. | **Open.** Needs a mechanical review check and a data fix of the review file. |
| 6 | A claim with one good and one fabricated evidence row printed `ok`. | **Closed.** Any failed row fails its claim (d828de8). |
| 7 | (Plausible) a claim with no evidence of its own passes on its parents alone. | **Open**, minor. |

Also found while fixing: `verify` does not check witness format on claim nodes
already in a store (only claims files are checked); a pdftotext footnote marker
glued to a word ("profiles92") makes a faithful quote fail the word-boundary
rule, a false failure kept on purpose (correctness first).

## Effect on this paper
`descartes check` (d828de8, binary sha256 `7cac773c…`, reproducible): 74 claims
ok, unchanged by the new rules. `stage1/article.sh`: inputs clean; Q007, Q048
and Q084 refused for citing raw HTML; both prompt digests match files at HEAD.

## Effect on Descartes's own claims
72 rows fail the prompt rule (interactive sessions and pasted transcripts, all
honest about having no prompt file), 8 fail as witness kind `model:`, and 1
faithful quote fails the word-boundary rule on a footnote marker.

## Decisions open (Sloane)
- Merge the branch, which requires migrating those Descartes rows and its loop's
  expected results (the Descartes owner).
- Run `descartes check` / `article.sh` as a gate in pre-commit and CI.
- A minimum quote length, and whether a quote may cross a paragraph break.

I had a read-only agent audit the whole checking chain for ways a wrong record could pass. It found seven and reproduced six; I've closed most of them. The Descartes fixes are on branch `witness-prompt-digest` (4 commits) and are not merged yet. The audit, finding by finding, is in `docs/audit-2026-11-04-verification-chain.md` and on trail #28.

**One live error in the paper, fixed.** Q022b quoted the RSP as "However, we will not", cutting off "necessarily delay", which is the word the claim depends on. It still passed the check. It now quotes the whole clause. That faithful quote fails on the PDF's line breaks, so the paper passes 74 claims, down from 75. Committed as `ceb603f`.

**Closed:**
- **Text on disk could be edited and still pass.** The audit appended an invented sentence to the Report's text, quoted it, and the check passed. The new verifier for paper repositories (`stage1/article.sh`) now refuses that. It checks every source against the manifest, re-runs every recipe and compares byte for byte, and refuses quotes taken from raw source files.
- **Quotes could pass while saying the opposite of the source.** Quotes now match whole words only, so "nnu" no longer matches inside "annually".
- **A fabricated row could hide behind a good one.** A claim now fails if any one of its evidence rows fails.
- **The witness rule could be bypassed by spelling.** Witness kinds are now a fixed set: `human`, `llm`, `org`, `doi` and `arxiv`. An LLM witness must name exactly one prompt, and the prompt file must be committed, not just sitting on disk. `LLM:`, a leading space, `llm-x`, `model:`, a second `prompt=` and untracked prompt files are all refused now.
- **The Descartes binary is reproducible.** Two builds from the same commit give the same binary, and the step record names the commit and digest that ran each check.

**Tests:** 153 unit tests, and 20 tampering cases for the verifier, each refused with its own message. A clean paper repository still passes all of them.

**Effect on this paper:** no passing quote was broken by the stricter rules. Three claims are now refused for quoting raw HTML: Q007 (the Delaware statute), Q048 and Q084. They need a recipe for rendered web pages before they can be cited.

**Effect on Descartes's own claims:**
- **81 rows fail.** 72 lack the prompt field, 8 use `model:`, and 1 is a faithful quote that fails because pdftotext glued a footnote number onto a word ("profiles92").
- **I kept the word rule strict anyway.** A false failure is visible; a false pass is not.

**Decisions for you:**
1. **Merge the branch.** That means migrating those 81 rows and the Descartes loop's expected results, which needs the Descartes session.
2. **Make the check a gate.** Nothing runs `descartes check` on commit or in CI. Today's hooks run only another session's `seal.py`, and those files are that session's uncommitted work, so I didn't touch them.
3. **Set two parameters:** a minimum quote length, and whether a quote may run across a paragraph break.

**Still open:**
- **The review file isn't checked.** Its labels don't line up with the claims file: 24 claims have no review row and 20 review rows have no claim, because labels were split or renamed. Most of its "verbatim" context passages don't match their source exactly.
- **Rows aren't tied to steps.** Nothing checks which step produced each claim row.
- **Stored claims bypass the witness check.** Claims already in a store, rather than in a claims file, aren't checked at all.

HTML_BLOCK = re.compile(r"^<(?:!--|/?[A-Za-z])")


def without_html_blocks(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Drop raw HTML blocks: as in CommonMark, a line starting with a tag or comment opens one, and the
    next blank line closes it. The Praxis writers print raw HTML as literal text, so web-only markup (the
    paper's figure gallery) stays out of these renderings."""
    out, skipping = [], False
    for line in lines:
        if skipping:
            skipping = line.strip() != ""
            continue
        if HTML_BLOCK.match(line):
            skipping = True
            continue
        out.append(line)
    return out


def compose(paper: Path, appendix: str) -> str:
    text = paper.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    lines = without_html_blocks(text.splitlines())

# The report as a build product

Status, 2026-11-04: the edition is one Praxis research report,
`edition/REPORT.md`, built by `scripts/build_edition.py` from
`edition/report.template.md` and rendered to PDF by the Praxis report writer.
The Marp deck (`DECK.md`, `deck/`) is retired: Marp needed Node and a headless
browser, and its styling was generic rather than the Praxis brand. The paper
template (edition v1 of the argument itself) is not built yet.

## Principle

The paper is not edited; it is **built**. An edition is a deterministic function
of one source commit and a few recorded parameters:

    edition = build(source commit, codebook version)

Rerunning the build at the same commit with the same parameters gives the same
bytes. The edition is then committed on top, so every edition names exactly the
code, data, codebook and prose it came from.

The **source commit** is the last commit that touched any build input (the
template, the build scripts, the codebook, `dag.lock.tsv` and every table the
build reads; `Build.inputs()` lists them), not HEAD. Committing the edition's
own outputs moves HEAD but changes no input, so the stamp and the generated
notice stay the same and `build_edition.py --check` passes on the edition
commit, in CI or anywhere else. The build already refuses to run when an input
is uncommitted or modified, so the source commit always describes the bytes the
build read. Any commit that changes an input (including a relock of unrelated
data, since `dag.lock.tsv` is an input) makes a new source commit, and
`--check` then fails until the edition is rebuilt.

The PDF is built, and it ends with a generated "Verification chain" appendix, Appendix F. Everything is committed and pushed. The appendix's headline result is **FAIL**: 74 claims pass and 22 still fail, every one of them listed with its cause.

**The PDF:** `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-srvo-dev-anthropic-pbc/c1e11076-829e-4b02-9641-6b48b095d475/scratchpad/render/anthropic-pbc-working-paper-5f76702.pdf`
- 28 pages, built from pushed commit `5f76702`. Two renders came out byte-identical.
- The document date is the paper's last commit date, not today's clock.

**What the appendix contains**, all produced at render time:
- **What built it:** the paper commit, the Descartes commit, and the SHA-256 of the binary that checked the claims.
- **A live verifier run:** 15 sources checked against the manifest, and 7 derived texts re-made and byte-identical.
- **The failing claims, grouped by cause:** three claims cite raw web pages (Q007, Q048, Q084), 19 quotes broken by PDF line breaks, and 4 quotes that occur twice in their source.
- **The step record:** which brief, by digest, produced which claims, at which commit.
- **The audit table:** each finding marked closed, partly closed or open.
- **The trails:** #25, #26 and #28. The appendix reads them from a committed snapshot, `docs/trails.tsv`, so rebuilding needs no Entire login. The snapshot holds only trails this repo cites, because the project's other trails have private titles.

**Every rendering does this now.** The render script (`scripts/render_report.py`) adds the appendix to any PDF or web page it builds from the paper, and AGENTS.md has a new rule saying so. The rule belongs in Praxis's producer contract too, so it covers every report. That file has another session's uncommitted edits, so I left it alone; it can go in once those land.

**Pushed:**
- **anthropic-pbc:** `ec-ai-corpus` is now on GitHub, 156 commits on top of `main`. Before pushing I confirmed that none of the blobs removed by the history rewrite is reachable, that no file is over 20 MB, and that the commits contain no credential patterns. Pull request link: https://github.com/srvo/anthropic-pbc/pull/new/ec-ai-corpus
- **Descartes:** `witness-prompt-digest` is pushed as a branch, not merged. The render needs that branch's `stage1/article.sh`.
- **Praxis:** the `ERRATA.md` commit is local only, because Praxis has no remote.

**Two loose ends:**

Commentary on the working paper, build 154d864

For anthropic-pbc-working-paper-154d864.pdf, which sits beside this note in the tray. Written by Claude on 2026-11-04. This note is not part of the build. I left the PDF unchanged because its Appendix F is generated, and typing comments into it would break that rule.

1. How to read the result line

Appendix F says FAIL. Here are the figures behind it:

CountWhat it is
97claim rows in claims/anthropic-contrapunctus.tsv, one label each
74claims that pass descartes check
23claims that fail descartes check
24claims that fail the whole chain. The extra one is Q007, which passes the check but is refused by article.sh because its evidence is raw HTML.

Correction: I told you "22 fail" in chat. That was wrong. 22 was the count from earlier runs, when the file had fewer rows. The right figures are 23 failing the check and 24 failing the chain. The paper doesn't contain the wrong number, because §5.3 points to the generated record.

2. What the failures are

None of these is a fabricated quote. Each is a limit of the instrument or a choice about which words to quote.

ClaimsCauseWhat would fix it
19: Q001, Q022a, Q022b, Q025–Q032b, Q050, Q052, Q062, Q064, Q066, Q070The words are in the source, but the text from pdftotext keeps the printed line breaks (and zero-width spaces in the RSP). For example, Q022b breaks at derived/rsp-v3.4.txt lines 1028–1030: "will not⏎necessarily delay".One general rule in Descartes on whether a layout line break matches a space (trail #26). The fix must never be made claim by claim.
2: Q010, Q013The quoted phrase appears more than once in the S-1.Either the editor picks a longer, unique span, or the check learns to narrow a match by section and page (the "where we find shit" item on trail #26).
2: Q048, Q084Anthropic's web pages contain each sentence twice (once in the page, once in embedded JSON). The check also refuses them as raw evidence.A recipe that works from a rendered capture of the page (trail #25).
1: Q007DGCL page, raw HTML, with no recipe yet.A recorded recipe. I haven't tested whether static-v1 accepts this page.

Q022b says something about the audit. The old quote dropped "necessarily" and passed. The corrected quote is faithful and fails on a line break. That swap is why the count fell from 75 (step S13) to 74 (step S14): the check got more honest, not worse.

3. Things in the PDF worth knowing

  • "The article verifier ran unsandboxed." The binary is reproducible: two builds came out byte-identical (7cac773c…). But the run happened outside the Descartes loop's sandbox. S13 also notes that rustup was reached through a mise shim, which the loop refuses. The result is real, but it hasn't been produced the way the loop would produce it.
  • The verifier is an unmerged branch. Descartes e7b3cb6 on witness-prompt-digest isn't on Descartes main. Until it's merged, the stricter rules (whole-word matching, any failed row fails its claim, closed witness kinds, raw evidence refused) only hold where that build is used.
  • Nothing enforces any of this yet (audit finding 1). No hook or CI job runs the check. The FAIL is visible only because the render runs the verifier. A commit can still land with a worse result.
  • Page 1 has an orphaned italic line: "Figures are generated deterministically…". It still needs your call.
  • The page footer reads "local review copy". That's right for now, but it has to change before any release.
  • Step S10–S11 edits say prompt=unrecorded. That's honest: they came from this interactive session, not from a committed brief. Q094–Q096 and the Q022b requote are circle-3 work with no prompt file.

4. Decisions waiting on you

  1. Merge Descartes witness-prompt-digest. Merging means migrating 81 of Descartes's own claim rows (72 have no prompt file, 8 use the model: witness kind, and 1 is a footnote-marker false failure) and the loop's expected results.
  2. Gate commits on descartes check / article.sh in pre-commit and CI. The hook files currently belong to another session.
  3. The line-break rule (item 1 in section 2). Settling it once would clear 19 of the 24 failures.
  4. Whether to set a minimum quote length, and whether a quote may cross a paragraph break.
  5. Whether model: is an alias for llm:.
  6. Whether to attach this PDF to a GitHub release.
